entries.name: FM-1 V15
entries.author: M-VAVE
entries.what: M-VAVE's official FM-1 firmware. It comes with the app, so you can always go back.

entries.name: SLOOP
entries.author: isod89
entries.what: A live groovebox: tracks, layers, a step sequencer, song mode, punch-in effects and samples, played on the FM-1 in real time.
entries.photoAlt: SLOOP 2.6 screens on the FM-1

entries.name: Felucca
entries.author: Leo Kuroshita (Hügelton Instruments)
entries.what: The custom firmware the others build on: the FM-1's own synth engines, a sequencer, effects and a better panel, with an editor in the browser.
entries.photoAlt: Felucca 1.0's feature overview: its new design, sequencer, thirteen engines, and effects

entries.name: JIANT FM
entries.author: juanjiant-bit
entries.what: A bio-synthetic groovebox: six tracks drawn as living beings in thermal colours, eight engines (FM6 with Dexed, analog, phase, voice…), mutating macros, song mode from SLOOP. Not yet tested much on a real FM-1.
entries.photoAlt: JIANT FM's reference sheet, with its screens and controls

entries.name: Skiff
entries.author: illuminus5
entries.what: Six tracks of synths and drums with a groovebox's workflow: fourteen engines, a 64-step sequencer with chords, ratchets, trig conditions and locks, songs, PERFORM with scenes, six themes and a browser editor; FM6 sounds built from scratch on the unit. Built on Felucca, with most of Felucca 1.6.1's work brought over (the second core, MIDI LEARN, INSERT); Felucca's sounds and projects load. Also runs on the SMK-37 Pro. Coming from 1.x: 2.0 saves in new formats – update on Skiff's own page (it backs up and converts), or back up in its editor first.
entries.photoAlt: Skiff's tracker and mixer screens

entries.name: Melodee
entries.author: keremimo
entries.what: Total playing pleasure, far beyond Felucca: recording without quantize, microtonal scales, a Casio CZ-1, a bit-by-bit Dexed, scale modes made for an MPC Sample as its companion.
entries.photoAlt: Melodee's Stage, Sounds, Notes, Mixer, Drums and Song screens

entries.name: X0X
entries.author: Charles Vestal
entries.what: A groovebox: 909 and 808 drums, two 303s with TB-3PO, a breakbeat generator and song mode.
entries.photoAlt: X0X's home screen, with the 909, 808, two 303s, and breakbeat patterns

entries.name: OberVave
entries.author: zvenson
entries.what: An 8-voice analog-style poly in the spirit of the classic American polys of 1979-84, now on four tracks: each its own sound, arp and sequence; a mixer with chorus, delay, plate reverb and drive sends, a master with DJ filter and compressor. Tracks start on the bar, patterns keep their sounds.
entries.photoAlt: OberVave's arpeggiator screen, with Arp, Div, Octaves, and Gate knobs

entries.name: Official Open
entries.author: M-VAVE
entries.what:
M-VAVE's own open-source firmware, which turns the FM1 into an eight-track groovebox: each track plays a DX7, 303, 808, PSG, Pluck, or sampler engine, with 16 USER project slots and an eight-slot sample bank every project shares. It installs from M-VAVE's FM1 Workbench, which also edits projects, simulates the device, and can put V15 back. This editor recognises it and sends it no Program Change or effect controls, which would change its tracks, but sends it no patches yet: a DX7 track takes a voice or bank downloaded from this editor as a.syx file, through the Workbench.

V14 holds 128 independent DX7 voices in four groups of 32 and takes DX7 single-voice and 32-voice bank SysEx.

Going back: the Workbench's Restore original V15 replaces all four banks with the factory voices, and a force flash may erase projects and samples, so download a backup from this editor first.
entries.photoAlt: Official Open's track screen: eight tracks, each with its engine and step row

entries.name: AMB-1
entries.author: Charles Vestal
entries.what: A generative ambient machine after Music for Airports: it plays itself from the start, breathing voices, bells on tape loops of unequal length, a gliding bass. You do not perform it, you tend it.
entries.photoAlt: AMB-1's Garden screen, with a chord ring labelled Dm7 and four knob readouts

entries.name: FMini-1
entries.author: Ruppert
entries.what: A three-oscillator monosynth in the spirit of the classic Moogs: a 24 dB/octave ladder filter, two contours, 100 factory patches, an arpeggiator, a sequencer and MIDI. Built on Felucca.
entries.photoAlt: Splash screen

entries.name: Clipper
entries.author: isod89
entries.what: A deep synth grown out of SLOOP: 23 engines and 407 sounds, from HYBRID (three oscillators, two filters, a mod matrix) to six-operator FM, wavetables, wave sequencing, a Juno and physical models; arp, step sequencer, MPE and a web editor for every parameter.
entries.photoAlt: Clipper for the M-VAVE FM-1: its screen

entries.name: ChoralRoot
entries.author: Quixotic7
entries.what: A Telepathic Orchid-style chord instrument: one hand plays roots, the other shapes chords; voicings, performance modes, bass and a looper.
entries.photoAlt: ChoralRoot's FM1 panel, showing a D major seventh chord on the screen

entries.name: GHOULBOX
entries.author: Jason Persinger
entries.what: Dungeon synth: a cathedral hall reverb, tape and crush, a hurdy-gurdy engine, choirs, organs and recorded psaltery and harp, an old-RPG screen with wall torches.
entries.photoAlt: GHOULBOX's skull title screen beside its home screen, with a hurdy-gurdy waveform between two torches

entries.name: GR!MM
entries.author: GR!MM
entries.what: Dark ambient, dungeon synth and deathdream firmware: 4 tracks, 7 sound sources, real recorded choirs, tracks that play by themselves, and long tape, granular and reverb effects.
entries.photoAlt: GR!MM on the FM-1: the HOME screen

entries.name: CoralFlower
entries.author: FicusFicusov
entries.what: Chords after the Orchid, with controls made for the FM-1: one key plays a chord with a bass note. Also 27 scales, an arpeggiator, a sequencer with drums and a song mode, and a pixel flower that grows as you play.
entries.photoAlt: A pink pixel flower growing and changing as chords are played

entries.name: Baud Girl (FM-1+VA)
entries.author: Baud Girl
entries.what: Keeps M-VAVE's FM engine and effects, fixes its engine bugs, and adds a Virtual Analog engine, an 8-Bit engine, a Bitcrush effect, a 64-step sequencer, and a Note Engine for arpeggios, auto-arpeggios, and auto-chords. It installs from Baud Girl's own browser page, keeps your presets, and can put M-VAVE's firmware back. This editor reads and writes its FM, Virtual Analog, and 8-Bit presets, effects included, keeps the 8-Bit ones in the library, and downloads them as presets files.
entries.photoAlt: Baud Girl's FM1 render, with her name on the screen

entries.name: Mutable Dreams
entries.author: Kid Bunka
entries.what: A generative instrument after a small modular setup: six freely assignable tracks, 15 engines (selected Plaits, Rings and Elements algorithms and voices of its own), 288 tones and 92 Biomes, 32-step phrases with live recording, chord journeys, a granular cloud and named User Banks. Plays and edits live in the browser.
entries.photoAlt: Mutable Dreams for the M-VAVE FM-1: its screen

entries.name: Tonitor
entries.author: Nuno Zimas
entries.what: Six tracks for live ambient and experimental music: three synth engines, patches generated by algorithm, free-length loops with up to ten overdubs each, a granulator, filters and a lush reverb.
entries.photoAlt: Tonitor for the M-VAVE FM-1: its screen

entries.name: FRASIL
entries.author: Styves Goupil
entries.what: An ambient drone instrument: tap a key to latch a drone, a note or a chord in your key. Three layers a voice into a big reverb with shimmer and freeze; GLINT's icy FM bells on top, by hand, arpeggio or sequence; BASS a deep line below, held or sequenced; three LFOs keep it all moving.
entries.photoAlt: The play page: the scene's name in the header, three drone voices as currents of ice in a river at night, the drone's mix below in four strata

entries.name: DUB-1
entries.author: sbegueria
entries.what: A generative dub techno machine that plays itself from the moment it is on: chord stabs into a tape echo, FM pings, a sub bass on five grooves, a ducking kick, crackle, and an eight-bar arrangement with breaks and fills.
entries.photoAlt: DUB-1's main screen, the Form page: Basic and FULL with the phrase's eight bar cells in the header, the stabs' ripples round the chord Fm7, the seven lanes below, FORM 1/3 on the rule and the knobs Energy, Vary, Motion and Drift

entries.name: Hortator
entries.author: DEADACTIVE
entries.what: A drum machine: eight tracks of drums, a step sequencer, Grids, a pumping compressor, LFOs, resonators and live effects. Play it in the browser first.
entries.photoAlt: FM-1 controls

entries.name: FoMni
entries.author: Charles Vestal
entries.what: A chord harp inspired by the Omnichord: strum the white keys, pick chords on the black ones.
entries.photoAlt: FoMni's strum screen, with the chord's strings and its chord buttons

entries.name: ZEN-1
entries.author: aceyprime
entries.what: Ambient as a living window: cherry petals on a river, koi in a pond, fireflies under a real moon, and every movement a note. Set it down and let it play; the keys play along, the knobs shape the scene.
entries.photoAlt: Sakura at night

entries.name: LOOM-8
entries.author: Charles Vestal
entries.what: A groovebox inspired by the OP-XY: eight tracks on nine engines, step tricks and locks, weave, a conductor and throws.
entries.photoAlt: LOOM-8 for the M-VAVE FM-1: its screen

entries.name: Fart Machine One
entries.author: adamcharleswilsonmusic-code
entries.what: A questionable musical instrument: ten artisanal farts, reverb, delay and a sixteen-step sequencer.
entries.photoAlt: Fart Machine One's screen, with a pixel-art character above reverb, delay, and repeat settings

entries.name: HYP-1
entries.author: RedtailWorks
entries.what: Hypnotic techno and acid: a breathing pad, a deep drone, a generative 303 line and grain over drums you sequence. Flip patterns on the bar, break it down, build it up. Forked from AMB-1. One of a pack of four: LOF-1 (a lofi groovebox), ECO-1 (a plant plays it) and GRAV-1 (a star and its planets), experimental, on its project page.
entries.photoAlt: HYP-1's panel on an FM1, with its home screen showing a chord ring

entries.name: Niagara Drift
entries.author: Evan Yerburgh
entries.what: A drone synth inspired by the SOMA Lyra-8, Moog Subharmonicon and Stylophone CPM DS-2. Two virtual-analog drones that breathe and drift on their own, with presets for instant ambient textures and full controls to push them into harsh, beating, self-oscillating sound.
entries.photoAlt: The FM-1 with what every control does in Niagara Drift written on it

entries.name: Rainbow Mode
entries.author: joshbartlettband-web
entries.what: A music toy for little children: 63 cartoon friends, every key in tune, chords, strumming, songs to follow and an ear game, notes on a staff, a volume cap for small ears.
entries.photoAlt: Rainbow mode's unicorn, one of its 40 friends, under a rainbow with its name below

entries.name: Ravel
entries.author: De-Pattern
entries.what: An eight-track groovebox for sound design: thirteen synth engines, struck percussion and 33 drum machines after the Machinedrum, on an influence grid where any track can trigger, excite or modulate any other.
entries.photoAlt: Ravel: sound exploration through texture. Custom firmware for the M-VAVE FM-1

entries.name: FM-106
entries.author: PatttF
entries.what: The Juno-106 emulation of KR-106 ported to the FM-1: six voices on both cores, the BBD stereo chorus, 128 factory presets and a 1980s Roland look.
entries.photoAlt: FM-106 for the M-VAVE FM-1: its screen

entries.name: SPAMPY
entries.author: Spampy-Droid
entries.what: SPAMPY 1.1: five-track synthwave FM-1 firmware with 170 synth presets, 44 drum kits including KAVINSKY, scenes, effects, 10 synthwave/atmospheric arpeggiators, extended envelope controls, corrected MIDI channel routing (no unintended synth or drum track triggering), dual-flash compatibility for…
entries.photoAlt: SPAMPY for the M-VAVE FM-1: its screen

entries.name: MONO2K
entries.author: Iñigo Hernandez
entries.what: Six mono machines in the spirit of Elektron's Monomachine: FM, superwaves, wavetables, a SID, a voice and four drum synths, one per track. A 64-step sequencer with parameter locks, trig conditions and ratchets, a lofi bus, four demo parts and a web patch editor.
entries.photoAlt: MONO2K for the M-VAVE FM-1: its screen

entries.name: NACHTFAHRT
entries.author: Cranky Man
entries.what: Generative 1970s Berlin School: two sequencers drift against each other over a drone, in eight endless pieces. Play a melody on the white keys and the lead answers it, takes it as its theme and grows new ideas from it.
entries.photoAlt: NACHTFAHRT

entries.name: zp12
entries.author: zvenson
entries.what: A 12-bit sampler after the E-mu SP-1200: sample on the FM-1 itself (a computer or phone plays into it over USB) or in the browser (mic, line-in or a file), and it plays on its own. Gritty and unsmoothed, with loops and songs.
entries.photoAlt: zp12's home screen, with A1 KICK on its LCD above eight channel faders and pads

entries.name: sloopDX
entries.author: zvenson
entries.what: SLOOP's live workflow with Dexed's DX7 engine and 128 steps a track: six operators, 32 algorithms, your own .syx banks, every voice edited on the FM-1, FM drums you program.
entries.photoAlt: sloopDX's banner: The FM-1, as a DX7, beside its algorithm screen

entries.name: fm1-dock
entries.author: Joakim Eriksson
entries.what: One firmware, many synths: hold HOME and pick CS-1, Scintilla (the Elka Synthex), OberVave or a sine, no reflashing. Add PROPHET, B3 ORGAN, Niagara Drift, ARTIHIVE, FM-106, FM-1 SID, AMB-1, FoMni, MONK-1, FiMba-1, GATOR, DUB-1, FMINI-1, FM6, ATEK303 or KEYS from the page with one click, and your…
entries.photoAlt: FM-106: the preset A85 Rocket Men, the VCF's sliders and the oscilloscope

entries.name: KARMA
entries.author: Ariel Muchnik
entries.what: A four-track groovebox: an acid bass or a Juno-style poly, physical modelling, two dozen synthesis models and a drum synth. A 64-step sequencer with song mode, generators that write parts on one chord plan, pixel characters, and USB audio with six stems, MIDI out and DAW sync.
entries.photoAlt: KARMA on the FM-1: the ACID track's screen

entries.name: ORBIT
entries.author: dspaudio
entries.what: A four-track groovebox: three synths and a drum machine in a colour-coded Synth, Drum, Event Tape and Mixer workflow, loops turned into songs, user macros, screens after the OP-1. Based on SLOOP.
entries.photoAlt: ORBIT's event tape: two reels above four tracks of notes, playing its demo

entries.name: Hortator (Bluetooth)
entries.author: DEADACTIVE
entries.what: Hortator's Bluetooth build: the same eight-track drum machine, plus Bluetooth MIDI for a BLE keyboard or clock, or the M-VAVE SMC-Mixer as a mixer for the eight tracks. Reads the plain version's projects.
entries.photoAlt: FM-1 controls

entries.name: Tessera
entries.author: Theo Dainis (Rastapopolix)
entries.what: Composing through systems on the FM-1. Thirteen generators, or your own steps, make parts that follow, answer and share one harmony. Sections, entries and a shape for the whole piece let a project unfold over minutes or hours. Play it by hand, or let it play.
entries.photoAlt: Tessera's logo above four of its screens: three of its generators and its mod matrix

entries.name: S1Vave
entries.author: Andrew GG
entries.what: An 8-voice virtual analog tweak synth: authentic 4-pole resonant filter, dual sub-oscillator, ADSR envelopes, 64-step sequencer, and hands-on live performance controls.
entries.photoAlt: S1Vave on the M-VAVE FM-1: PTN 1-01, PERFORM page with CUTOFF, RESO, ENV AMT, PORTA T, real-time scope, 7-segment display, and 8-voice LEDs

entries.name: FiMba-1
entries.author: jadamsowers
entries.what: A physically modelled kalimba: tines laid out like the real one, thumb-roll chords, mbira patterns, a sound hole to cover, grains, tape and a plate reverb. Play it in the browser first.
entries.photoAlt: FiMba-1's tines screen, with the kalimba's tines, its chord buttons, and its Material, Hardness, Decay, and Tone

entries.name: CS-1
entries.author: twochannels
entries.what: A Yamaha CS-80 in spirit: eight voices of two channels, high- and low-pass filters in series, ring modulator, the touch response and 22 tones from the owner's manual. A sound module played over MIDI.
entries.photoAlt: CS-1 for the M-VAVE FM-1: its screen

entries.name: Dinghy
entries.author: zvenson
entries.what: Your base for your own FM-1 or SMK-37 firmware: everything under it done and documented (updates, USB rescue, MIDI over USB and the TRS jack with clock, USB audio, keys, screen, flash storage, an update screen), a 4-voice sine on top, tests and a CI that releases with attestation. Fork it, replace the sine.
entries.photoAlt: Dinghy's screen: the name, the note played, a keyboard with the keys that sound

entries.name: FuMi-1
entries.author: cartesive
entries.what: A shigin conductor after the Suiko ST-50: its two rows of keys, the key set in honsū, equal or its own just tuning, a koto and twelve more sounds on a 6-op FM engine, ring time, vibrato, trill and a looper.
entries.photoAlt: FuMi-1's play screen, with the koto chosen, its name in kanji, and the ST-50's keys

entries.name: MAKU
entries.author: okumurari
entries.what: An ambience machine for DJ interludes: switch it on and a random world in key plays, four parts, buttons that are verbs, and the worlds you like breed new ones. Clock follow. Play it in the browser first.
entries.photoAlt: MAKU's pulse screen, with a waveform and a mix of four voices

entries.name: Jangada
entries.author: zednaked
entries.what: Dark, industrial, Brazilian: drones that breathe, ten engines (6-op FM, a superwave analog with a ladder filter), four tracks, a mod matrix, live effects.
entries.photoAlt: Jangada's tracks screen, with four tracks in magenta

entries.name: RemoteFM1
entries.author: Quixotic7
entries.what: A firmware for your firmwares when using the app or a high quality 24bit DX7 rompler with 16 user carts and MIDI Controller when using the FM-1 by itself. BLE and USB supported!

entries.name: Golana
entries.author: Gadlele
entries.what: One analog-style synth laid out like the classic microKORG, with a screen that draws the sound.
entries.photoAlt: Golana's power-on animation

entries.name: fm1-chord
entries.author: math0ne
entries.what: A chord machine after the HiChord, with extras: chords in a key under the white keys, slash chords and inversions, sounds, envelopes, effects and a looper.
entries.photoAlt: fm1-chord's home screen, with the chord C7 above a keyboard

entries.name: FMEL-1
entries.author: Antonio Altea
entries.what: Mellotron-style tape sounds, coloured with effects and lo-fi tape: flutes, strings and choirs as on the old tape frames, played from the keys.
entries.photoAlt: The choir tape

entries.name: PERF-1
entries.author: deamonSLINKY
entries.what: A groovebox that plays itself while you steer it: nineteen genres, FM pad, bass, acid and pluck voices, drums with a step sequencer, an auto-DJ, effects you play on the keys, scenes, and a Jam page to play along. Store your pieces, and share them through the online library.
entries.photoAlt: Three screens: the home screen (a summoning circle that turns to the chord's root and draws the chord), the master bus page (the compressor's curve, the limiter and the output meter) and one of the visualizers.

entries.name: Frodhes
entries.author: Leonardo Mirabal
entries.what: An electric piano, vibraphone and marimba, physically modelled, no samples, with drive, tremolo or wah, phaser, chorus, delay and reverb (hall, plate, infinite), tap tempo and MIDI clock sync, an arpeggiator, a sequencer, scales and presets.
entries.photoAlt: Frodhes on the FM-1: the FRODHES page, four cards for the four knobs

entries.name: Polly
entries.author: Charles Vestal
entries.what: A pocket arranger after the QY70: pick a style, play three keys for a chord and a band of eight follows, songs from sections, General MIDI sounds from Sonivox EAS, and a General MIDI module over MIDI in.
entries.photoAlt: Polly for the M-VAVE FM-1: its screen

entries.name: Caravel
entries.author: BonszaiMusic
entries.what: Multi-engine synth firmware with DRONE, STASIS texture capture, Pair Morph, and per-track Random Morph and Morph Journey for evolving, ambient and experimental sound design. Sequencer, MIDI Learn, USB audio.
entries.photoAlt: Caravel tutorials: learn the FM-1 step by step. Open the tutorials.

entries.name: DARK-1
entries.author: Polystellarflow
entries.what: Dark-music firmware for the FM-1: 21 genres, 210 pieces, dark techno to dark ambient and darkwave. Wander evolves it on its own. Arp, Dice, step editor, new visuals, simpler settings, bigger text. Works on older and newer FM-1s (both flash chips).

entries.name: Arctic Scream
entries.author: PolarPatch
entries.what: Long dark screaming ambient from the frozen Arctic. A living feedback loop creeps out of the cold and grows into a howl, ice sings when struck, wind drifts over the tundra. Four tracks, ten sound sources, endless reverb and shimmer. Let it play whole pieces by itself through the eight Sami seasons.
entries.photoAlt: The Arctic Scream demo: the FM-1's panel in the browser, ICE WRAITH playing

entries.name: DUELL
entries.author: OSCILL/R
entries.what: A MULTIMORPHING bitimbral synth: two complete parts, three ways to play them together, and a morph that glides between two versions of every sound. Ten engines with wavetables, twin filters, effects and a mod matrix. Macros and MIDI presets for Circuit Tracks and MPC/Force. Velocity, aftertouch.
entries.photoAlt: The DUELL card: a multimorphing bitimbral synthesiser by OSCILL/R

entries.name: K-WASUB
entries.author: Omnipotard (Guizmoh)
entries.what: Runs on the latest FM-1 chip. A bass synth for DnB, dubstep, dub and techno: deep subs, reese, growls and 808s. Two of nine engines play together, the keys change the wobble live, and one button plus a knob puts an LFO on any setting. With drums, a bass sequencer and live FX pads.
entries.photoAlt: K-WASUB, a modern bass synth for the M-VAVE FM-1

entries.name: Optimist
entries.author: w0ts
entries.what: A modular firmware built on SLOOP, Felucca, Melodee, X0X, and other FM1 projects: you choose its engines, drum kits, effects, and features in a browser builder with a live flash and RAM budget, try the build in a simulator, and install it from the same site. Its releases come in ready-made flavours; 0.3 adds Ableton Link and SD card support, and its new memory layout erases projects saved in flash, so back them up in the web editor first. Its README calls it early access and says it runs on real FM1s while most features are tested in the emulator and on a computer.

entries.name: Chipbox
entries.author: pbarilla
entries.what: A ultra-refined Chiptune music editor, featuring over 35 classic chips such as NES, Gameboy, heck even the Sunsoft 5B! Pages with their own meter, tempo and glide, so waltzes and 7/8 grooves are easy. Gimmick fans rejoice!

entries.name: KAWA
entries.author: Omnipotard
entries.what: A pocket tracker for chiptune and IDM: six tracks of pulse, 4-bit wave, noise, 6-operator FM, drum kits and samples. Chain patterns into songs, chop breaks, and play 64 live effects (with K-GLITCH's DESTROY and BEAT), a filter and an FX sequencer.
entries.photoAlt: KAWA, Pocket Tracker for the M-VAVE FM-1

entries.name: Mini-Tone
entries.author: Stéphane Schmitz
entries.what: Felucca with six tracks and new engines: SID, Braids' 48 models, a TB-303 and engines after Elektron's Analog Four, SY Chip and Digitone 2, a ping-pong delay and a new reverb. Built on Felucca 1.5.
entries.photoAlt: FM-1 controls with Felucca

entries.name: Guru-600
entries.author: Marc Massé
entries.what: The FM-1 becomes a Prophet-600: 255 sounds (the 100 factory programs, 100 from the free 2022 collection, 55 of its own), a web editor in 7 languages with a panel inspired by the Prophet-600, four tracks with sequencer, arpeggiator, morph and two insert effects each. Based on Felucca.
entries.photoAlt: Guru-600's HOME screen: its filter readouts above a ring of coloured bars

entries.name: NOIZ DEMONS
entries.author: SPIKE the Percussionist
entries.what: Felucca with randomization as a ritual: every new sound summons one of 30 demons of the Ars Goetia, its sigil takes the screen and its rank decides how wild the sound gets.
entries.photoAlt: The NOIZ DEMONS boot splash

entries.name: M-PYRE
entries.author: History Of Sky
entries.what: A riffbox for rock and metal: real guitar, bass and drum samples, an amp engine with cabinet IRs, pedals and guitar effects, plus all of SLOOP's synth engines. Bend strings, play whammy, wah and palm mutes live, record on the 4-track and turn riffs into songs.
entries.photoAlt: TRACKS: the four tracks and their steps

entries.name: Demake
entries.author: Sequencist
entries.what: An ambient lofi machine on 64 of its author's own pedal recordings: three synths, each with a piano roll, eight patterns, its own reverb, delay or tape echo and motion; huge shared reverbs, colour and old media over the whole mix; a chord machine and an arpeggiator, sixteen scenes, a song mode.
entries.photoAlt: Demake on the FM-1: Home, synth 3's landscape

entries.name: CTL-1
entries.author: Charles Vestal
entries.what: A MIDI controller: notes in any scale with its chords on the black keys, four banks of knobs, an arpeggiator and Euclidean drums, with General MIDI sounds of its own when nothing is connected.
entries.photoAlt: CTL-1's play screen, with a keyboard, USB and TRS switches, and four controller knobs

entries.name: ECHOFIELD
entries.author: PhilipsKnobs
entries.what: A granular sampler: a few seconds of any sound become slow clouds, sparkles, tape loops and swells, played from the keys and knobs. 14 factory sounds, your own samples (or recorded over USB), filter, delay, reverb and tape, and a companion web app for samples, presets and recording.
entries.photoAlt: ECHOFIELD, a granular sampler firmware for the M-VAVE FM-1

entries.name: winampFM Synth
entries.author: Hericdk
entries.what: Winamp 2.x on the FM-1, built on SLOOP: your sounds as a playlist, four tracks you record as loops, effects on sliders and a visualizer made of lines. The real firmware plays in a 3D simulator first.
entries.photoAlt: winampFM Synth for the M-VAVE FM-1: its screen

entries.name: Elixir
entries.author: Dan Majka
entries.what: Deep drum synth and sequencer that ports the Erica Synths LXR-02 and adds 22 more sound engines, generative sequencing, extensive randomization & modulation, live performance tricks, MIDI control of 300 parameters with Launchpad and Launch Control maps (see website), and 8-channel USB audio.

entries.name: MNM-1
entries.author: Veff
entries.what: Six monophonic tracks of synth and FX machines, pages of eight knobs, a filter and a tape delay on every track, three LFOs a track, parameter locks and slides. Forked from Hortator, with sounds ported from MONO2K.
entries.photoAlt: MNM-1 for the M-VAVE FM-1: its screen

entries.name: WaveLoop FM-1
entries.author: ELI7VH
entries.what: Felucca played from an Arturia MiniLab 3: track faders, a DJ filter, momentary effect pads; 32 patches a bank, 12 evolving songs, revoiced 808 and CR78 kits.
entries.photoAlt: Felucca 1.0

entries.name: MONK-1
entries.author: Charles Vestal
entries.what: Twelve singers, from Jerry the monk to Snider the punk, each in its own voice: MonkSynth's formant voices, played with velocity and pressure from the FM-1's own keys.
entries.photoAlt: Jerry the monk singing, mouth wide open, in front of mountains and prayer flags

entries.name: FM1 Quest
entries.author: Hericdk
entries.what: A pixel-art RPG while you make music, built on SLOOP: four heroes, one a track, walk through a village and fight monsters and bosses as your loop plays, every SLOOP screen redrawn in the game's style.
entries.photoAlt: FM1 Quest's title art: a pixel-art party of heroes around an FM1 in an autumn forest

entries.name: Carnac OS
entries.author: OrbVorgis
entries.what: CARNAC OS is a dual-timbral wavetable synth inspired by neolithic monuments and forgotten rituals. Built for deep sound design and immediate control, with a MAQ 16/3-style sequencer and a J6-style chord arp. The PCM waves need a separate installer: get it from my GitHub page.
entries.photoAlt: Carnac OS for the M-VAVE FM-1: its screen

entries.name: Shine On
entries.author: zvenson
entries.what: A string ensemble in the spirit of the late-70s machines, grown out of OberVave: divide-down keyers with 16', 8' and 4' footages, register filters, a BBD ensemble and a phaser per sound. Now on four tracks with a mixer, delay, reverb, drive, a master and the step sequencer.
entries.photoAlt: Shine On's screen: program 01 ENSEMBLE, the PERFORM page with four knobs, the scope, sixteen keyer LEDs

entries.name: Amenity
entries.author: Presethead
entries.what: A live jungle tool built around classic breaks (Amen, Apache, Think) and your own. Hold white keys for rolls, builds, echo and Akai-style metallic stretch, play hits on the black keys, and shape the break with variation, warp, ringing feedback, lo-fi, EQ, saturation and compression.

entries.name: Bigorna
entries.author: Nuno Zimas
entries.what: Rhythmic noise, power noise, industrial and IDM after the Elektron Digitone II: six tracks, four machines (4-OP, DRUM, WAVY, HIVE), parameter locks on a 16-step sequencer, a looper, send effects and USB audio.
entries.photoAlt: Bigorna for the M-VAVE FM-1: its screen

entries.name: Penumbra
entries.author: Lunar Eclipse Forge
entries.what: An ambient space-drone synth that plays itself until you do. Drone voices drift in and out, a far-off voice sings, and the sound glides from scene to scene as an eclipse crosses the screen. Every key is in tune, and loops follow each key change. A thick, slow drone, like the Solar 42.
entries.photoAlt: Penumbra: the Lunar Eclipse Forge mark in an eclipse's corona

entries.name: FM Lab
entries.author: jsmith13
entries.what: A six-operator FM synthesizer made for learning FM: no drums or song mode, just the DX7 engine with every parameter under a knob while the sound plays, and a screen that shows what you changed. It has eight voices, 32 user slots, a small arpeggiator and a one-phrase looper, and is built on Dinghy. Its README says it runs on the FM1, and it installs from its release package.

entries.name: Vector37
entries.author: genkigenki
entries.what: An orbiting overtone synth: four corners of two overtone generators each, a sun on a path and a moon around it decide how much of each you hear; the knobs shape the selected planet. Made for the SMK-37, here its FM-1 build. After the Beetlecrab Vector.
entries.photoAlt: Vector37: an orbiting overtone synth for the SMK-37, its orbit screen

entries.name: Bubba Machine
entries.author: Erbubar23
entries.what: A six-track groovebox written from scratch: TR drums from Plaits' 808 and 909 models, a sampler with a 16-slice slicer, a bass and three free tracks (analog, 6-op FM, 303 acid), scenes and fills, all at 44.1 kHz.
entries.photoAlt: Bubba Machine's home screen, listing machines BR-8, BP-1, and BB-303 with their step patterns

entries.name: PurpleMonkey
entries.author: Quixotic7
entries.what: A first instrument for toddlers: random key bashing and knob turning are rewarded with dancing animated pets and little musical sequences. Press a key, any key.
entries.photoAlt: screens

entries.name: SLOOP DX7 Banks
entries.author: majnikool
entries.what: SLOOP 2.4 with up to twelve DX7 voice banks, kept and named in the editor, presets by kind. Test builds: back up first.
entries.photoAlt: SLOOP 2.3 screens on the FM-1

entries.name: TRIBE
entries.author: apiel
entries.what: A ten-track groovebox where any engine plays on any track: kicks, 909 and 808 voices, the 303, sixteen clips a track, scatter effects and four master knobs you assign. Built on X0X.
entries.photoAlt: TRIBE's start screen: TRIBE Sound System, 10 tracks, any engine, based on X0X and AMB-1

entries.name: Blop
entries.author: Obsimo
entries.what: Explore sound with your Blop: one-finger chords from 38 grids, chord rhythms, a bass with its own riffs and a few discreet drums with sidechain, while a little creature swims to your chords in an aquarium on the screen. Chords and bass go out as MIDI over USB.
entries.photoAlt: Blop for the M-VAVE FM-1: its screen

entries.name: Pocket GammaWave
entries.author: ShadowTune (GammaWave Audio)
entries.what: The companion to the GammaWave desktop synth: four industrial distortions, vowel and scream filters, an FFT spectrogram, a four-track tape deck screen and a song generator with 49 genres, trap and drill too.
entries.photoAlt: Pocket GammaWave (GW-1) Hardware Screens

entries.name: FM1-GM
entries.author: jartificer
entries.what: A General MIDI sequencer with 16 tracks, 128 General MIDI instruments to choose from and a drum kit (on track 10). It can store up to 64 songs, each containing up to 128 measures.
entries.photoAlt: FM1-GM: the logo above a white FM-1 panel, with thumbnails for 128 sampled GM sounds, the 16-track sequencer, 64 song slots, the web song editor, the browser emulator and the 5 colour themes

entries.name: AISLING
entries.author: CU_STE
entries.what: Irish ambient music that plays itself for ever: harps, flute and drone. Eight pieces to steer, or play along on its keys, a keyboard or a DAW. Now an app on your iPhone too, no FM-1 needed. Its visualiser paints the music as an Irish landscape.
entries.photoAlt: AISLING: a gold 8-bit harp on green

entries.name: VESPER
entries.author: Fat Cat Studios
entries.what: An ambient worship synth. Each scene layers four lush voices in any major key around a crystal orbit home screen: pads, plucks, piano and swells. Shape them with drive, tone, granular clouds, shimmer, reverb and delay, then play live over the scene or record into it.
entries.photoAlt: VESPER: the startup screen, and the home, FX and envelope pages in the Ember, Forest, Mono and Crystal themes

entries.name: Saadet
entries.author: keremimo
entries.what: A synthesiser fork of Melodee, by its author, with Bluetooth MIDI and 24-bit audio. Its 1.0 has six engines, among them a PPG Wave and a three-oscillator HYDRA, two parts, factory libraries, and a web editor, and the project also builds for the SMK-37. Its README called 0.1 experimental, with checks of the exact release package still pending. It installs from its own browser page.

entries.name: Kitten Synths
entries.author: Black Kitten Devices
entries.what: NEW: six tracks and USB recording of all of them. Four synths (one a Minimoog-style MUUG with 100 sounds, plus a light LITE synth), two drum kits, 12 drum pattern templates in the web editor. Works on both FM-1 flash chips (old and new). A SLOOP 2.8 groovebox with songs, punch-in FX and USB MIDI.
entries.photoAlt: Kitten Synths

entries.name: DRIFT
entries.author: FBNFRTG
entries.what: An ambient instrument for live sessions: warm synths, spacious pads and delicate plucks over a generative Euclidean sequencer on one track, with delays and reverbs from spring to shimmer. Built on Felucca.
entries.photoAlt: DRIFT sequencer

entries.name: ETCH
entries.author: Joppe Sikken (SikkenWorks)
entries.what: Draw your own waveforms, morph between sounds, and bring them to life with modulation, evolving textures, and powerful effects. From warm analog-inspired tones to wild experimental soundscapes, ETCH puts sound design right at your fingertips.
entries.photoAlt: ETCH for the M-VAVE FM-1: its screen

entries.name: Tuna
entries.author: delirioux
entries.what: Generative music for the FM-1: it composes as it plays, melody, bass, accompaniment and percussion shaped by music theory out of controlled randomness. Pick a composer or one of 86 genres across eight decades and it plays in that manner, endlessly and never twice the same.
entries.photoAlt: Tuna for the M-VAVE FM-1: its screen

entries.name: SIDOU
entries.author: Denis Sablić
entries.what: Turns the FM-1 into a C64 SID machine: two SIDs measured on real chips, a GoatTracker 2 tracker and sequencer with swing, Euclid and ratchets, .sid playback and .sid to song, LAB with tables and LFOs, AI-made songs and sounds, SidStation banks, Bluetooth MIDI and keyboards, Live Link and scene art.
entries.photoAlt: Eight screens of SIDOU on the FM-1's LCD: the boot title, LIVE playing a song with the keys on chip B, the TRACKER, STEP, the CHIP view, the RED MOON RITE scene, an ORDER list and an instrument page

entries.name: Arcturus S6
entries.author: Zeptosecond DSP
entries.what: An experimental, self-playing wavetable instrument for generative, evolving soundscapes. Four PPG-style oscillators, Serge-style function generators, sample-and-holds and logic, patched through mod and gate matrices. 12 bit, 22kHz, green phosphor CRT, Fairlight-style pages.
entries.photoAlt: Arcturus S6's boot screen

entries.name: No Man Sky FM
entries.author: Hericdk
entries.what: A space adventure while you make music, built on SLOOP 2.7.1: fly between planets with two knobs, land, mine, fight sentinels and warp between stars, every SLOOP screen floating over the game.
entries.photoAlt: No Man Sky FM for the M-VAVE FM-1: its screen

entries.name: MIN-1
entries.author: Reytian
entries.what: A tiny minimalist ensemble after Philip Glass: it starts playing when you switch on, you join whenever you like. In EASY mode every white key is a chord that fits. Four models, twenty pieces.
entries.photoAlt: MIN-1 in the browser emulator: the FM-1, and its screen at twice the size

entries.name: FM-1 NES
entries.author: Keitark
entries.what: Plays NES games on the FM1: its 27 keys are the controller and its screen the television. It is the worked example in a kit for writing FM1 firmware from scratch, published as source with no installer page or ready-made release, and no game included. It makes no music.

entries.name: Bunker Evolved
entries.author: Kid Bunka
entries.what: Generative ambient: four editable layers from 64 sound recipes, 24 worlds, 24 motifs and 32 scales. GROW varies the phrases, seven EVOLVE processes change them over time. Felucca's sound pages stay. Built on Felucca 1.6.1.
entries.photoAlt: Bunker Evolved for the M-VAVE FM-1: its screen

entries.name: CHOPPAH
entries.author: Laurens Profittlich
entries.what: An Amen break chopper for the FM-1: eight classic breaks cut into 16 slices on the white keys, hold a key to loop it. Black keys are momentary pads for rolls, reverse, freeze, tape stop, gate, filter and dub throws. A generator rearranges the break live, with a four-slot FX chain and a DJ filter.
entries.photoAlt: CHOPPAH's slicer screen: the break cut into sixteen slices, with the playhead and the slice window

entries.name: PT/FM
entries.author: hitosu
entries.what: A ProTracker-style pocket studio: DX7 FM, JUNO-106, TB-303, chip, sampler and FUSION instruments side by side, 16 voices on both cores, a loop station, a two-deck DJ mode, punch-in effects and over 500 built-in instruments.
entries.photoAlt: STATUS, the start screen: POCKET TRACKER / FUSION MACHINE, BY HITOSU

entries.name: ARTIHIVE
entries.author: KHAV
entries.what: Eight-voice experimental drone and polyphonic FM synthesizer with four interacting pairs, envelopes, legato glide, hyper LFO, stereo motion, dual modulated delay and a 1-16 step arpeggiator and sequencer. Artistically inspired by SOMA LYRA-8; independently developed.
entries.photoAlt: artihive-logo-640x320-byKHAV

entries.name: Felucca [Salt]
entries.author: Chance Roth (ChanceTheMaker)
entries.what: Felucca with a hardware-inspired Studio in the browser (play it there without an FM-1): many engines, presets, skins. A beta.
entries.photoAlt: Felucca Salt Studio in Stage Red, with browser audio and oscilloscope

entries.name: Smileyface
entries.author: pbarilla
entries.what: You're making acid, baby! Smash that LFO button until you hear something you like, and then twist those knobs! Now with 100% more FX! A truly trippy experience! Built on Chipbox.

entries.name: sloop-DUB
entries.author: altessproduction
entries.what: a four-band isolator with mute bands, a bipolar DJ filter, per-track echo throws, a tape echo and a siren voice. The bank: 180 genre presets, 38 kits and 27 riddims of the Riddim Collection grid (African Beat, Real Rock, Sleng Teng), each loading its four patterns: bass, skank, the rest, drums.
entries.photoAlt: The FM-1's TRACKS screen under SLOOP Dub, playing

entries.name: J6
entries.author: JackieAlacrity2373
entries.what: A six-voice JUNO-60 style polysynth with chorus, arpeggiator and a 16-step recorder. 56 factory sounds, a MIDI control for every knob, and a free browser editor that plays it over USB-MIDI.
entries.photoAlt: J6 screen

entries.name: SLOOP Floyd FM
entries.author: René Bohne
entries.what: SLOOP with a visual four-operator FM engine after Floyd Steinberg's 4-OP idea: an ADSR per operator, seven pages, a live oscilloscope that draws the envelopes as you play.
entries.photoAlt: SLOOP 2.3 screens on the FM-1

entries.name: X0X-RMX
entries.author: Mr-Roboto (Oliver)
entries.what: X0X remixed after The Orb: banks and patterns reordered live per voice, Grids MAP and EUCLID drum generation, an extended TB-3PO with 22 scales and a morphing 303 waveform. Built on X0X.
entries.photoAlt: X0X running on the FM-1 (watch on YouTube)

entries.name: MYCELIUM
entries.author: Mandalars
entries.what: Forest, Psytrance, Goa and Hitech grooves, built on Felucca and SLOOP: original drums and icons and four factory songs. A test release: not yet fully tested on the device.
entries.photoAlt: MYCELIUM running on a real FM-1

entries.name: PIGEON
entries.author: The Shrimp Blimp
entries.what: An old-school hip-hop and house sampler after the SP-404 and the PO-33: two song samples and a 16-pad kit, up to 32 chops a song, a 64-step sequencer, patterns and a song arrangement. Built on Felucca.
entries.photoAlt: PIGEON for the M-VAVE FM-1: its screen

entries.name: Araminta
entries.author: Wulgaren
entries.what: A fork of Felucca 1.5.1 that adds JIANT's DRUM-X drum kit and punch-ins, free-take recording from Sloop, a mixer solo, an effects list you chain or send, and, since 3.0, a WAVETABLE engine. It installs from its own browser page, which can also put M-VAVE's firmware back.
entries.photoAlt: Araminta's boot screen, a white flower drawn in dots on black

entries.name: Felucca 8 Patterns
entries.author: echoe
entries.what: An LLM-written expansion of Felucca with eight patterns per track, pattern chaining (up to 512 steps/pattern), per-step patch switching, multiple new chord modes, generative arpeggiator, new synth engines LEAD and SH-DRUM, borrowed engines SWARM, FM-TONE, and WAVETONE from Mini-Tone, new effects…

entries.name: Rhythmer
entries.author: Jazzy Rhythmer
entries.what: A hands-on groovebox firmware for the FM-1. Shape sounds, build patterns, and find your own groove. Up to six assignable tracks, sound design, sequencing and performance. Free and open source, built on JIANT and reworked by Jazzy Rhythmer.
entries.photoAlt: Rhythmer — Sound into motion. Startup and Break screens from the FM-1 firmware.

entries.name: Drumlab
entries.author: pbarilla
entries.what: Microtonic, for the FM-1! Roll the dice for a kit, build one from scratch, or bring in your Microtonic presets and patterns. Share kits and patterns as files, and send it all to your Teenage Engineering PO-32! Built on Chipbox!

entries.name: Scintilla
entries.author: Joakim Eriksson
entries.what: The 1981 Elka Synthex on the FM-1: all 80 factory sounds, Paul Wiffen's laser harp among them, checked sample by sample against the original. Two layers of 8 voices (single, split, double), poly, mono or unison, chorus and reverb, and the four knobs edit what is on the screen.
entries.photoAlt: Scintilla on the emulated M-VAVE FM-1, playing the Laser Harp (Ring mod.) with laser beams above it

entries.name: MC-1
entries.author: dspaudio
entries.what: An original four-part groovebox with a 1990s workflow: three melodic parts and a 16-lane drum part, 128 melodic presets, eight drum kits, song arrangement, an arpeggiator and recorded knob moves.
entries.photoAlt: MC-1 home: four pattern rows, note pitches and playback cursor

entries.name: Del Rio
entries.author: Jess Del Rio
entries.what: A rhythm box of ceremony percussion: djembe, cajon, udu, clapsticks, maracas and triangle, their real strokes on the black keys, a step sequencer on the white keys and 31 rhythms from the literature. Played alone: a berimbau with its caxixi, a buzzing tanpura and a breathing shruti box. Built on fm1-base.
entries.photoAlt: Four of the firmware's screens: the djembe's steps in HEARTBEAT, the capoeira's bateria in RODA ANGOLA, the gunga's SOUND page, and the tanpura playing

entries.name: Bytemania
entries.author: lloyd (llozd)
entries.what: A bytebeat synth: play one-line formulas, tweak them with the knobs, and write your own, with a random button in the formula creator that is really fun. A beta, built on Dinghy.
entries.photoAlt: The main screen

entries.name: 386DX
entries.author: seajaysec
entries.what: A karaoke robot with a band: it sings songs from karaoke and MIDI files, or lines you type, to the notes you play. Its face is the voice. Keys, bass and drums play along, with a step sequencer and sixteen punch-in effects.
entries.photoAlt: The 386DX trailer

entries.name: Cut-A-Dor
entries.author: Kid Bunka
entries.what: A beat dojo for scratch DJs and beatmakers: boom bap, lo-fi and breaks from 16 rhythm families with swing and fills, an eight-lane 32-step sequencer, punch-in effects you record bar by bar, a bass voice. Sound banks and editor in the browser.
entries.photoAlt: Cut-A-Dor for the M-VAVE FM-1: its screen

entries.name: fm1-radio
entries.author: Charles Vestal
entries.what: An internet radio over WiFi: it joins a 2.4 GHz network, plays stations from Radio Garden's map, and puts punch-in effects on the keys. Its first release, 1.0, was withdrawn after crashing on some FM1s when WiFi started; 1.3.1 is a pre-release, whose notes ask anyone whose FM1 crashes to report it. It installs from its own browser page, with a manual on the same site.

entries.name: NCC – Novation Circuit Companion
entries.author: Fenderberg
entries.what: Turns the FM-1 into a two-part synth for the Novation Circuit Tracks: parts L and R follow MIDI 1 and 2 on split outputs, played from the Circuit's knobs. Twelve engines from DX7-style FM to Juno, CZ, acid and granular, 161 sounds, synced arp, drone and effects. Works with any MIDI keyboard too.
entries.photoAlt: NCC running in the browser emulator, on a purple FM-1

entries.name: GuitChordi
entries.author: Stoogs
entries.what: A chord and string instrument: 16 synthesized sounds, 50 chord styles, editable voicings, guitar tunings, and Freeplay, Strum and Arp modes with partial-chord pulses.
entries.photoAlt: GuitChordi for the M-VAVE FM-1: its screen

entries.name: HADAL-1
entries.author: Polystellarflow
entries.what: Generative dark ambient: drones, demonic and angelic choirs, bells and 135 sound effects that keep changing by themselves across 15 worlds, with 40 melting pictures. Play bells or latch choir voices on the keys, or play and hold effects. Works on older and newer FM-1s (both flash chips).

entries.name: FOMAJAM
entries.author: konsumer
entries.what: A drum machine in the classic step-grid style: voices after the 909, 808, 707, 606, DMX and more, a machine per voice, accents and patterns. Play it in the browser first.
entries.photoAlt: FOMAJAM playing a 909 pattern

entries.name: Skiff Atlatl
entries.author: LIkst4
entries.what: A six-track groovebox for the FM-1, forked from Skiff: a SYNTH with analog, 303 and Plaits-style oscillators, an acid filter and OberVave presets, a Minimoog voice, classic drum models, more trig conditions, a step arpeggiator, 8-channel USB audio, a web editor and screen mirroring.
entries.photoAlt: Skiff 1.3 on YouTube: the FM-1's second core, 12 voices, MIDI LEARN

entries.name: BBL JAM BOX
entries.author: UnkleBlairy
entries.what: A live-jamming groovebox in the style of the Digitone and Model:Cycles, modified from Felucca. It has six tracks with 16-step sequencers, parameter locks, a four-operator FM engine, 808-style drums, and a sampler for your own sounds, and installs from its own browser page.

entries.name: NCC
entries.author: fenderberg
entries.what: Novation Circuit Companion, a Felucca fork that turns the FM1 into a two-part synth for the Novation Circuit Tracks: part L plays the Circuit’s MIDI 1 track and part R its MIDI 2, with twelve engines and 161 sounds picked by role, and the Circuit’s eight macro knobs mapped to each engine’s parameters. It has no sequencer of its own: the Circuit plays the notes and sends the clock. It installs from its own browser page, which can return the FM1 to V15.

entries.name: Patchwerk
entries.author: Matt Kuebrich
entries.what: A modular synth for the FM-1. With over 80 modules, including synth engines, samplers, filters, effects, sequencers, and generative tools, you can build, patch, and perform directly on the hardware.
entries.photoAlt: Adding a filter after another module

entries.name: winampFM
entries.author: hericdk
entries.what: A firmware in the style of Winamp 2, based on SLOOP 2.6: sounds become a playlist, four tracks record as loops, effects sit on sliders, and 28 visualisers fill the screen. It installs from its own page, which runs it in a 3D simulator first.
entries.photoAlt: winampFM for the M-VAVE FM-1: its screen

entries.name: MOPE-1
entries.author: slothpallas
entries.what: A sad wavetable synth played by a pixel blob in a rainy room: its eyes are the filter, its mouth the envelope, its tears the delay. Gloomy beats with auto-bass, an arpeggiator, a pattern sequencer, twelve punch effects on the black keys, and presets of your own.
entries.photoAlt: the blob, through its parts

entries.name: TastyWaves
entries.author: marksweiss
entries.what: A 12-voice wavetable synth: two oscillators a voice, a resonant filter, two envelopes, an LFO, four effects, an arpeggiator and two step sequencers for chords and counterpoint; load your own Serum, WaveEdit, Ableton or Surge tables.
entries.photoAlt: The power-on animation: waves crash and TastyWaves rises out of the splash

entries.name: April OS
entries.author: beashoko
entries.what: A Felucca fork for sampling, kept deliberately simple: 32 sample slots of three seconds each, an eight-track sequencer, a sample and loop editor, and recording through a computer's or iPhone's microphone, bridged by its own page. It installs from that page. Its repository holds the page, not the firmware's source.

entries.name: FM-1 firmware patcher
entries.author: czietz
entries.what:
A script that changes your own copy of M-VAVE's V15 or V16 rather than a firmware of its own: operator detune matches Dexed, aftertouch no longer brings a strong vibrato, and the main screen's scope turns dark blue. The FM1 still reports V15 or V16, so this editor treats it as M-VAVE's firmware.

The patched file may not be shared, so you run the Python script yourself. M-UPGRADE sees it as the V15 already installed, so go down to V14 with M-VAVE's tone updater first, then install it; the same steps put V15 back.

entries.name: GammaWave
entries.author: fvalente
entries.what: A synth firmware based on Felucca, with a wavetable sound, a live spectrogram filter, a four-track tape deck, and a song generator with 49 genres. It has a web studio and installs from its own browser page.
entries.photoAlt: GammaWave for the M-VAVE FM-1: its screen

entries.name: JAN3000
entries.author: JanSchulten
entries.what: An OP-1 and OP-Z-inspired Felucca fork: four tracks, sixteen scenes per project chained into songs, two lanes of FX tracks with live punch-in effects, J-6 chord sets, and engines that include a Volca Drum-style drum machine, an 808, five after Plaits, and a TB-303-style bass. It installs from a local page in Chrome or Edge, and a manual in English and German is online.

entries.name: OG Synth
entries.author: mikejohnsonbeats
entries.what: A synth firmware by Mike Johnson Beats with 16 engines, 28 effects, and four tracks that play at once. It installs from the browser installer on its site, which links a backup of your presets first, and the site carries a manual and a version history. Only the application part of its source is published, under MPL-2.0; its sound engines, effects, and sequencer are proprietary.

entries.name: TransitFM1
entries.author: Quixotic7
entries.what: A tiny firmware, by ChoralRoot's maker, to stop at between two others: it makes no sound and stores nothing, answers installers as M-VAVE's V15, and carries ChoralRoot's flash safeguards, so an install cut off part way brings the FM1 back in update mode. Its README says 0.1 worked on an FM1, and 0.1.1 fixed two bugs seen on one. It installs from its own browser page or its release package.

entries.name: BEETLE
entries.author: Joppe Sikken (SikkenWorks)
entries.what: BEETLE transforms the FM-1 into a powerful 6-channel music workstation. Create beats, design sounds with retro-inspired synth engines, sequence entire songs, and perform with live effects. A complete pocket-sized tracker, drum machine, and synthesizer. Built for creativity, born out of passion.
entries.photoAlt: BEETLE

entries.name: Kitten Rack
entries.author: Black Kitten Devices
entries.what: A Eurorack-style modular synth: 57 modules (VCOs, a chord VCO with arpeggiator, a Moog-style ladder, a Moog 960-style sequencer that plays your voices, a low pass gate, Turing, Marbles, chaos, effects) patched with cables on the FM-1 itself, a 64-step sequencer with live recording, 33 factory…
entries.photoAlt: Kitten Rack: the patch's modules as Eurorack panels, with their cables, on the FM-1's screen

entries.name: Trumpagotchi
entries.author: Trust This Mechanism
entries.what: An unofficial parody virtual pet with a playable pentatonic keyboard. Feed, praise, clean up after and rest the pet. When he's happy, he joins your playing on bongos.
entries.photoAlt: Trumpagotchi controls

entries.name: Matryoshka
entries.author: michael glaviano
entries.what: A modular synth for the FM-1: 30 factory patches built from nested modules, from classic polysynths to drum machines, each played with four knobs per page, plus a step sequencer with patterns and songs. Build your own patches in the browser editor and send them to the FM-1 over USB.
entries.photoAlt: Coral and yellow parent dolls with two teal siblings, connected by matching cable arms

entries.name: Sill
entries.author: delirioux
entries.what: Generative 90s eurodance, pickled in 1995. Press PLAY and Sill writes a song and plays it: offbeat basses, piano and supersaw stabs, a chorus hook with a choir and a key change for the last chorus. Ten styles; steer it with four knobs, break it down, push the key up and play the hook yourself.
entries.photoAlt: PLAY: the chords, the bar as it plays, the song's form

entries.name: Loom FM-1
entries.author: Co-oscillator
entries.what: Four synth and sampler tracks and a drum track on 14 engines, among them wavetable, 6-op FM, tape scrub, granular and a slicer; a 64-step sequencer, a chord progression generator, macros and sidechain ducking.
entries.photoAlt: 5-Track Mixer

entries.name: MODELAR
entries.author: Hirakos
entries.what: A semi-modular drone synth played like a Kaoss Pad: four oscillators modulating each other through eight routings, and keys that move a cursor on an XY pad instead of playing notes: white keys are points, black keys gestures. ARP, a polymetric sequencer, a clock in Hz and eight generative environments.
entries.photoAlt: The KAOS PAD screen

entries.name: ESTAMPIE
entries.author: Drew Robinson
entries.what: A groovebox for lively mediæval dance music: hurdy-gurdy, lutes, shawms and frame drums over drones, four tracks with 64-step sequencers, mediæval modes and temperaments, and velocity from the FM-1's own keys. Built on GHOULBOX and Felucca.
entries.photoAlt: ESTAMPIE: the M-VAVE FM-1 playing the TROTTO in its vellum look, on an illuminated page with vines, ivy leaves and the calligraphic Estampie wordmark

entries.name: HERA
entries.author: Ben Badio
entries.what: A chord groovebox after the Roland J-6: 100 chord sets, 9 phrase styles with 12 variations each and a 64-pattern step sequencer, on a four-voice Juno-style synth from Clipper with chorus, delay and reverb. A chord map on the screen shows which chord sits on which key. Built on Dinghy.
entries.photoAlt: Every HERA page on the FM-1 screen

entries.name: OPN-1
entries.author: putchdev
entries.what: The Sega Genesis / Mega Drive's Yamaha YM2612: six channels of 4-operator FM. Its web app takes patches from game music (VGM) and OPM files and streams VGM tunes to the FM-1 to play.
entries.photoAlt: The FM-1 play screen: patch B1 04, its algorithm and the sound knobs

entries.name: JAMTRACK
entries.author: PhilipsKnobs
entries.what: A backing band to play over: drums, bass, chords and a synth line follow your chords in any key and time signature, in time with a loop pedal. 160 factory jams in 16 genres, a new jam at a press, your own synth line on a piano roll, and a companion web app to edit and share jams.
entries.photoAlt: JAMTRACK on the FM-1: the chord playing, the progression, the band

entries.name: FIZZ
entries.author: Quixotic7
entries.what: A groovebox around one engine, ChoralRoot's FM TONE: six tracks, p-locks and preset sound locks, conditions, ratchets, chords, and MIDI FX for generative patterns and for reworking the ones you have. Bluetooth MIDI, and recording over USB audio.
entries.photoAlt: FIZZ's logo, the letters in blue, green, orange, and pink among drifting coloured bubbles on black

entries.name: Nauclerus
entries.author: Mr. Roboto
entries.what: Hortator's eight-track groovebox taken further: ORB Remix with 256 pattern mappings, the TB-3PO acid melody generator with 22 scales, more acid waveshaping, four bipolar LFOs and Grids rhythms copied into editable steps.
entries.photoAlt: Nauclerus

entries.name: PALEOTONE
entries.author: fantasmoslam
entries.what: A prehistoric groovebox, formerly called DINOBOX: since 8 Nov it carries the earlier PALEOTONE's roaring creatures, drones and war drums on RAPTOR's base, SLOOP 2.8.4 built on Felucca, with six tracks and a demo song. Its README now gives a backup and recovery note in place of its early-alpha warnings. It installs from its own browser page, which also plays it in an emulator, and has a manual.

entries.name: PurpleMonkey FM-1
entries.author: Quixotic7
entries.what: A first instrument for a small child, by ChoralRoot's author: press any key and something nice happens. Every key is a note on a five-note scale or a drum, over a backing beat, with four animal friends on the screen and no menus. It installs from its own browser page and plays in a browser first.
entries.photoAlt: A grid of PurpleMonkey's pixel-art screens, each with an animal character

entries.name: SY1
entries.author: fenderberg
entries.what: A polysynth by NCC’s maker that plays Synth1 patches (.sy1), with Synth1’s 99 parameters under its own numbers: two oscillators and a sub, FM, ring and sync, filters, three envelopes, two LFOs, an arpeggiator, unison, and effects, with 256 community presets built in and a bitimbral mode on the FM1’s second core. Its README says it installs and runs on one FM1. It installs from its own browser page, plays in a browser first, and has a patch manager.

entries.name: XMOD
entries.author: Kot Morderca
entries.what: A MOD / XM tracker, sampler and groovebox: play, write and save FastTracker 2 and ProTracker songs on the FM-1, up to 32 channels, with a ProTracker mode for MODs and a song manager in the browser for moving songs to and from the computer.
entries.photoAlt: The splash screen

entries.name: GATOR
entries.author: ivanvoid
entries.what: A monophonic macro-oscillator on the open Plaits DSP: all 24 models with harmonics, timbre and morph, an 8-slot mod matrix fed by an envelope, two LFOs, velocity, aftertouch and random, a low-pass gate, and a DRONE mode.
entries.photoAlt: GATOR

entries.name: Daurade
entries.author: delirioux
entries.what: Grooves in chrome: filtered, pumping, robotic. Press PLAY and Daurade plays a filtered loop that opens over sixteen bars, a mix that pumps on every kick, a robot voice singing the hook and crisp drums. Ten styles; steer it with four knobs, drop it, set off a solo or play the lead yourself.
entries.photoAlt: PLAY: the chords, the filter's sweep, the pump

entries.name: CULTBOX
entries.author: beatcult
entries.what: A three-channel groovebox: a Polivoks-style duophonic synth (PLVKS), an Elka-style sample drum machine with a step sequencer, and a dub siren, with BBD echoes, per-channel character effects, arp, scales and a mixer with panning.
entries.photoAlt: The MIX page

entries.name: B1
entries.author: Joppe Sikken (SikkenWorks)
entries.what: B1 turns the M-VAVE FM1 into a compact drawbar rock organ with 91 shared tonewheels, nine drawbars per registration, percussion, Leslie, B3/ROCK tones, MIDI and expressive live controls.
entries.photoAlt: B1 drawbar organ on the M-VAVE FM-1

entries.name: SID-1
entries.author: putchdev
entries.what: The Commodore 64's SID chip, twice for six voices. Its web app edits patches and takes them straight from .sid game music files.
entries.photoAlt: The FM-1's SOUND page: SWEEP PAD's pulse wave, its filter and the main knobs

entries.name: FMER
entries.author: Nacsez
entries.what: Six-operator FM and Virtual Analog synthesis with four-track sequencing and songs. FMER Companion, a Windows app, installs it and keeps instruments, projects, and backups on the computer, with DX7 import and export. Build 736 adds Bluetooth MIDI between two FM-1 units.

entries.name: Ripple
entries.author: charlesvestal
entries.what: Runs instruments written in Lua over sounds written in Faust or C, copied to the FM1 as a USB drive with nothing to reflash, after monome's norns. Its site plays it in a browser, installs it, and has a manual, and its emulator has a panel for writing your own.

entries.name: Berlinan
entries.author: Jiří Píša
entries.what: A generative Berlin School MIDI sequencer: a small ensemble of voices that repeat, phase against each other on loops of unequal length and earn their mutations over time. The FM-1 makes no sound with it: each voice goes out over USB on its own MIDI channel to your synths, as Berlinan for macOS…
entries.photoAlt: Berlinan for the M-VAVE FM-1: its screen

entries.name: LUXR
entries.author: HOLODECK AUDIOTOOLS
entries.what: An LXR-style drum machine: eight sounds, each a synth and a sample layer, with drive, delay, reverb, filter, compressor and limiter. 16 patterns of up to 64 steps, per-track speed, locks, conditional trigs, chains and song mode, MIDI clock and CC learn. Its samples are the Sonic Potions LXR's, non-commercial licence.
entries.photoAlt: LUXR for the M-VAVE FM-1: its screen

entries.name: Manifold
entries.author: stets43
entries.what: Generative just-intonation firmware for the FM-1. Two layers of moving points wander a map of 41 scales and play the notes they pass; a rhythm without a grid drives four drums that follow the synth. Four knobs steer it, the keys play into it, and it can stream to Bluetooth speakers.
entries.photoAlt: The Perform page

entries.name: PULHRA
entries.author: 646timur-cell
entries.what: A minimal Elektron-style groovebox: four tracks, patterns in banks A to E, parameter locks, trig conditions, chains, an arpeggiator per track and per-pattern kits on the MONOFM sound core. A hard fork of Felucca.
entries.photoAlt: PULHRA for the M-VAVE FM-1: its screen

entries.name: bocjuhn
entries.author: ryuji kanagawa
entries.what: A six-track instrument for sound exploration and live layering. Eight engines span FM, acid bass, textures and hybrid drums. Shape sounds with granular processing, filters and effects; record free loops, build sequences, add automatic accompaniment and morph between snapshots. Based on Tonitor.
entries.photoAlt: bocjuhn for the M-VAVE FM-1: its screen

entries.name: Unholy Union
entries.author: actuallysparky
entries.what: Generative ambient and drone: Immaculate Permutation rolls an arrangement in one key, a pad, a sequence and a chord arpeggio under a fourth voice for your hands. Keep a sermon you like, evolve it, or reveal another.
entries.photoAlt: Unholy Union for the M-VAVE FM-1: its screen

entries.name: Evander's Music Box
entries.author: Michail Tsakiroglou
entries.what: A bard's instrument for LARP, medieval and high fantasy: recorder, hurdy-gurdy, harp and a tavern kit on four tracks, encounters and songs for the table. "Mother Melody hears thy song."
entries.photoAlt: Evander's Box Web Emulator Interface

entries.name: LOAF BREAKER
entries.author: FLEXOR
entries.what: A hardcore kick synthesizer powerhouse (gabber, terror, speedcore) and a breakbeat chopper (Based on CHOPPAH) : twenty kicks with distortion, sliced breaks, effects, drums, songs with drops, a BEGINNER mode, a DAW-like Studio on PC. The editor adds up to 8 breaks: yours or from a library of 90+.
entries.photoAlt: CHOPPAH's screens: the splash, the start screen, the slicer view, playing, a slice held, a roll

entries.name: Argo
entries.author: echoe
entries.what: An LLM-written expansion of Felucca with eight patterns per track, pattern chaining (up to 512 steps/pattern), per-step patch switching, multiple new chord modes, generative arpeggiator, new synth engines LEAD and SH-DRUM, borrowed engines SWARM, FM-TONE, and WAVETONE from Mini-Tone, new effects…
entries.photoAlt: Argo's feature poster, listing its engines and effects

entries.name: Modular One
entries.author: bunglesociety
entries.what: Film-music firmware built on Felucca. Its README says it runs on the author's FM1 and has not been tested on other units. It installs from its release package.

entries.name: VIBE FM Link
entries.author: zvenson
entries.what: Play the VIBE FM VST plugin with your FM-1. Install this and the FM-1 is the controller: the keys play, KNOB 1-4 and every button do in the plugin what they do on the FM-1 – SLOOP, Felucca, OberVave and the other converted firmwares feel like home, in your DAW, in the Web Player and on the VIBE FM. The sound comes from the plugin, not the FM-1. Plain MIDI: any synth or DAW can learn it too.
entries.photoAlt: VIBE FM Link for the M-VAVE FM-1: its screen

entries.name: B3 ORGAN
entries.author: R-Jeb
entries.what: A B3 tonewheel organ computed from setBfree's own data: 91 wheels, drawbars for three manuals, key click, vibrato and chorus, percussion, overdrive, reverb and a Leslie. All 110 setBfree programs, 16 of your own, and a web editor that reads and stores the FM-1's sound.
entries.photoAlt: The three screens: upper, lower and pedal manual (the pedal screen also shows the load and the MIDI input)

entries.name: SPELLBOX
entries.author: Philippe Jaccoud
entries.what: SPELLBOX turns the FM-1 into a talking spelling toy after the 1978 Speak & Spell: an 8-character fluorescent display, a 10-pole LPC voice at 8 kHz through an 8-bit DAC, and the SPELL, LETTER, SAY IT, SECRET CODE and MYSTERY WORD games over four levels, with the keys as an A-to-Z keyboard. SPEAK…
entries.photoAlt: SPELLBOX for the M-VAVE FM-1: its screen

entries.name: Veffbox
entries.author: Veff
entries.what: Resampling sound design. Build one sound from FM, analog or 808-style drums, play it as notes, steps or strummed chords, add 6 LFOs, 3 envelopes and 8 FX, then resample it into a new source. Every resample keeps its recipe, so a 64-sound bank of generation trees rebuilds bit for bit.

entries.name: SATIE-1
entries.author: OCKM Studio
entries.what: Erik. Evolved. Ten Satie pieces become an evolving electronic soundtrack in five moods. Choose a tune, set the pace and blend Solo, Duet or Trio. Shape each instrument, add vinyl colour and synced delay, or simply let it play. GLO opens the quick guide.
entries.photoAlt: SATIE-1 cover

entries.name: Fantasma
entries.author: Gadlele
entries.what: An ambient firmware forked from Felucca, which keeps all of its engines and adds a Pad that writes its own chords, bells that play themselves, an endless noise engine of sea, rain, or vinyl, and an Omnichord on the keys. It installs from its own browser page.

entries.name: Gnomad
entries.author: kpalaniuk
entries.what: Easy, kid-friendly firmware built on Felucca, with sound pictures instead of menus, four colour knobs, and a singing gnome. It comes as a release package, installed with a Python script.

entries.name: MIDIMON
entries.author: ignis32
entries.what: A MIDI monitor for USB, the TRS jack and Bluetooth (as device and host at once): hex or words, filters, stats. Its THRU routes, each filtered, make the FM-1 a Bluetooth MIDI dongle.
entries.photoAlt: LOG: messages from USB, TRS and both Bluetooth links, in hex and in words

entries.name: SIREN
entries.author: isod89
entries.what: A rave that writes itself, a firmware made from Clipper and SLOOP. Its README calls 0.10 experimental: it passes its tests on a computer and is being tested on the FM1. It installs from its browser installer, with SIREN STUDIO beside it, and can go back to V16 or V15.

entries.name: Speak37
entries.author: genkigenki
entries.what: A talking synth, written for the SMK-37 and built for the FM1 too: every key speaks the next word at its pitch, chords speak in harmony, and MOPE, a gloomy robot, says what he thinks of what you play. Its README asks for feedback on how it plays on the FM1. It installs from the SMK37 page’s FM-1 tab.

entries.name: Trireme
entries.author: ignis32
entries.what: Turns the FM1 into a macro keyboard that VIAL configures, keeping its settings in flash. It stays a USB MIDI device, so the usual firmware installers still reach it. It installs from its release package.

entries.name: DX747
entries.author: Esben von Buchwald
entries.what: An eight-part multitimbral DX7 module. Every part has its own MIDI channel and up to eight layered DX7 voices, with key splits, velocity windows and 64 scenes. A master filter, shared reverb and delay, DX7 ROM import and a web configurator. Played and controlled over MIDI.
entries.photoAlt: DX747's start screen: a jumbo jet above the name, with the words 8-part multitimbral DX7 module

entries.name: FM-FAM
entries.author: David Amo
entries.what: Dfam style 16-step sequencer and a drum synth: two oscillators with 16 wave types, a kick with its own sequencer, parameter locks, a sound saved per pattern, an effects chain, random pages, scales, presets and projects.
entries.photoAlt: SEQ: Step edit

entries.name: hawk-chua
entries.author: plieuwski
entries.what: Noise and modeling synth with GM-style presets (4 banks, 512) and a 4-track tape recorder: each voice a live Chua circuit or noise program, through vactrol gates into resonators and piano, drum, voice, flute, brass, bowed, reed and bird waveguides, with temple, cathedral and mosque reverbs. GM…
entries.photoAlt: HAWK CHUA on the FM-1

entries.name: Dungeon Tracker
entries.author: Bourbon Weather
entries.what: Four Track Groovebox with a dungeon crawler cooked into the home screen for the visualizer. Create your party from 8 heroes, store up to 6 sequences then string them together in Song mode!
entries.photoAlt: Dungeon Tracker for the M-VAVE FM-1: its screen

entries.name: Ombak
entries.author: Lunar Eclipse Forge
entries.what: A gamelan-inspired ensemble. Lead the core melody on the white keys and the ensemble answers: interlocking kotekan, reyong, kendang and gongs in measured Balinese and Javanese tunings, every note shimmering with ombak. Play the traditional forms, or slow it right down for meditation.

entries.name: SiDJ
entries.author: thomasj (tubesockor)
entries.what: Plays C64 SID music from HVSC on an emulated 6581 or 8580 and lets you remix every voice live: transpose, mute, solo, swap waveforms, bend envelopes and filter, add LFOs, ride the tempo. Out of the jack, as USB audio or over ASID to a real SID. MIDI clock from the tune, or the tune synced to yours.
entries.photoAlt: SiDJ playing Commando, voice 1 an octave up

entries.name: Yehnah
entries.author: Mello-D
entries.what: Six-track groovebox firmware with 25 synthesis engines, 800+ presets and no samples. Chord layouts you play with one thumb, a 64-step sequencer, idea generators, songs with arrangement, SWARM, TRACE and XYZ sound-morphing pads, a browser editor and emulator.
entries.photoAlt: Yehnah's start-up screen: the name drawn in pink over a pixel-art city, a small robot in front

entries.name: Makohai
entries.author: delirioux
entries.what: A generative groovebox in the style of early-90s PC tracker music. Six lanes (lead, arp, pad, bass, drums and sfx) play parts composed live in eighteen styles. You don't program steps, you mix styles: blend the next one in lane by lane, shape each lane with tracker effects and call the drop.
entries.photoAlt: Makohai's screen: the VOLUME setting, all six lanes of notes scrolling past a fixed play line, and the four knobs' values for lead, pad, bass and drums

entries.name: Agent Deck
entries.author: kevinelliott
entries.what: Turns the FM1 into a desk controller for coding agents running on a computer, with their states on the key lights and the screen, driven by a program on the computer. Its README says 0.3 runs on its author’s FM1, and 0.6 adds light cues, context gauges, and more sounds. It installs from its release package, plays a scripted session in a browser emulator, and no licence is stated.

entries.name: AGTDECK
entries.author: Kevin Elliott
entries.what: A control surface for coding agents, not an instrument: the keys and screen show which of your Claude Code, Codex or other command-line agents are working, finished or waiting on you, and the buttons approve, deny, interrupt and prompt them. It needs its daemon on the computer.
entries.photoAlt: An FM-1 in White and Blue running Agent Deck. Its screen plays through the firmware: the splash, waiting for the host, the GRID with a blocked agent calling, DETAIL with the prompt, INFO and DIFF, APPROVALS and ALL CLEAR, the GRID as boxes, the MENU and ABOUT

entries.name: B1 Drawbar Organ
entries.author: SikkenWorks
entries.what: A drawbar organ, by BEETLE's maker. Its README says B1 has been installed and tested on a real FM1, including booting and sound output, and its release package comes with a browser installer.

entries.name: FM-1 Chimera Vocal
entries.author: Shan-Sherif
entries.what: A singing human voice for the FM-1, ported from Jameson Hodge's CHIMERA. A simulated airway (lungs, vocal folds, throat, mouth, nose) sings words a syllable per key, or holds vowels you shape with the knobs. Write the words in the browser Studio and send them over USB.
entries.photoAlt: The FM-1's screen singing Hello there, I am a voice made of air, a syllable a key: the head moving, the syllable sounding and the next

entries.name: FM-1 Macropad Patch
entries.author: smememe
entries.what:
A patcher, not a firmware, which changes your own copy of M-VAVE’s V15 so that every button, key, and knob sends a USB-MIDI note, fourteen buttons, 27 keys, and seven knobs each way, which an app such as Keyboard Maestro or MidiKey2Key turns into shortcuts. The synth functions go, and so does the settings screen, so set the velocity you want with M-VAVE’s firmware before patching.

The patched file may not be shared, so you download V15 yourself and patch it in the web page or with Python, then install it with M-UPGRADE. Its README says no recovery method is known if an update fails; M-VAVE’s updater puts V15 back.

entries.name: FM-1 MIDI Processor
entries.author: MidiHax
entries.what: A stand-alone MIDI processor, with no computer needed. The synth is removed, so the only sound is a metronome click. MIDI from TRS and USB goes through a pipeline and comes out of USB, with a searchable monitor showing what it did to each message, per-port channel and message filters, and message and channel remaps. Event triggers send a list of messages, such as the bank and program changes for a whole rig, from one incoming message. The knobs send CCs, the keys play notes and send program and bank changes, and clock lockout keeps clocks from being merged. It holds 16 named patches, which can be dumped and loaded over SysEx, and it is built on the Official Open V14 source. Latency measured on an FM-1 averages under 0.2 ms. It installs from its own page in desktop Chrome or Edge over USB.
entries.photoAlt: FM-1 MIDI Processor's MIDI monitor: a table of incoming messages by port, channel, type, and data

entries.name: FM1 Audio Router
entries.author: MAX RAVE
entries.what: USB audio interface and Bluetooth audio receiver with FX
entries.photoAlt: Mixer screenshot

entries.name: FM1 Keyboard Academy
entries.author: chmess
entries.what: A first keyboard course: eight chapters from finding middle C, twelve exercises, and thirty traditional melodies, each played to you, lit on the keys, and listened to, with the FM synthesiser and its DX7 presets still behind the learning screen. Its README says the preview has been installed on an FM1 and the whole course still needs playing through. It installs from its pre-release package.

entries.name: JAZZY OS
entries.author: JazzyRhythmer
entries.what: A sound-exploration instrument on Rhythmer and JIANT, with 31 engines and over 1,200 factory sounds, one sound to a track, a step sequencer with automation, GEN for drafting parts, the Amen and Think breaks, and USB MIDI host. It installs from its own browser page and plays in a browser.

entries.name: SLOOP ALG
entries.author: shaw-core
entries.what: An experimental fork of SLOOP 2.2 that adds engines of its own: a six-operator DX7 that imports DX7 voices, virtual analogue, additive, pluck, and Karplus-Strong strings, each editable on the FM1. It installs from its own browser page and has its own web editor for sounds. Its notes are in Chinese.

entries.name: Jam Playground
entries.author: Bob Perry
entries.what: Jam Playground plays a new song the moment you turn the FM-1 on. Four synths and eleven drums sound together. Turn a knob to change the vibe, the scale, a sound, or an effect, and play along.
entries.photoAlt: Jam Playground for the M-VAVE FM-1: its screen

entries.name: KRIECHSTROM
entries.author: Grigorii Bezborodov
entries.what: Dark industrial and EBM on the FM-1. Feedback that howls in tune, a sidechain pedal that pumps, crushes or talks through a vocoder, strings that ring with the mix, tape cut and glued back wrong, the GLCH distortion engine and 179 sounds.
entries.photoAlt: KRIECHSTROM

entries.name: CLATTER Pocket
entries.author: allmyfriendsaresynths
entries.what: A generative drum machine on the LXR sound engine. Seven voices, kits grown from a seed in 16 characters, a 64-step sequencer with conditions and per-step pitch, patterns generated and mutated in 11 styles, MIDI notes and clock in, and nine named projects.
entries.photoAlt: The Pocket panel, rendered by the host tests

entries.name: RUPTURE
entries.author: Joppe Sikken (SikkenWorks)
entries.what: A monophonic bass synth on Cycle Exchange Synthesis: two sub-oscillators, a ladder filter, Channel EQ, eight effects from MOSFET drive to octave fuzz, a step sequencer up to 128 steps and an arpeggiator.
entries.photoAlt: RUPTURE for the M-VAVE FM-1: its screen

entries.name: FM1-TRAX
entries.author: jartificer
