entries.what: A Mega Drive / Genesis music tracker. It emulates the YM2612 and SN76489 chips: six FM channels, three square waves and noise, with Deflemask-style effects, 128 FM presets, a drum kit on the DAC, 256 song slots, a demo song and VGM export.
entries.photoAlt: Various views of the FM1TRAX firmware, with the intro screen at the center

entries.name: Flyfish
entries.author: delirioux
entries.what: One piece on the FM-1: Chopin's Etude in C major, Op. 10 No. 1, on a sampled Steinway D. Flyfish plays it and lets you shape it, practise it and move it.
entries.photoAlt: HOME: the étude falling as droplets

entries.name: Adrift
entries.author: Romain Guy
entries.what: Adrift transforms the M-VAVE FM-1 into a 16-voice, 6-part Bucket-Brigade Resonator synthesizer, capable of plucked guitars, bowed cellos, buzzing sitars, granular clouds, hands-free drones, and massive unison leads.
entries.photoAlt: Adrift logo

entries.name: ATEK303
entries.author: Animatek
entries.what: A TB-303 style acid synth with its own pattern generator: press PLAY and a line plays. Generate, mutate and undo patterns up to 64 steps, edit steps in a piano roll, add drive, chorus, synced delay and plate reverb. The ATEK303 engine from VCV Rack with 14 oscillators and its fine tuning, 12…

entries.name: Demake synth
entries.author: InigoHernandez
entries.what: An ambient lo-fi machine, by MONO2K's maker, built on 64 recordings made with pedals and played by three synths, each with its own piano roll, patterns, and chain of lo-fi effects, with scenes, a song, and a chord machine leading them. It installs from its own browser page or its release package, and plays in a browser first.

entries.name: Felucca MPE
entries.author: stanleygurvich
entries.what: A fork of Felucca 1.6.1 that adds MPE support, a per-voice LFO and a DRIFT source for chords that move and breathe. It installs from the.fwsc package committed in the repository. Its README says it has only been tried in the browser emulator and never installed on a real FM-1.

entries.name: FIENDBOX
entries.author: emilystgeist
entries.what: A demon synth for dark, occult music, from old JRPG dungeons to dungeon synth: a GHOULBOX fork, itself built on Felucca, with ideas and code from JIANT FM. It adds five power-on scenes, a creature drawn for each engine on its edit pages, and bytebeat and floatbeat waves for the LOFI engine. Its README says it has been tested on one FM1. It installs from its own browser page and has a web editor.

entries.name: L/RRY
entries.author: OSCILL/R
entries.what: A stereo-field morphing synth. Two oscillators with eight models, a sub, noise and ring mod, two filters and two dirt stages, each with its own pan. Move the pans and the sound travels around you. A morph glides between two versions of every patch. Effects and a mod matrix. Best with headphones.
entries.photoAlt: The L/RRY card: a stereo-field morphing synthesiser by OSCILL/R

entries.name: LCD-4
entries.author: devrvega
entries.what: A pocket groovebox: four tracks, a drum machine and three synths, playing 16-step patterns that chain together, with 808, 909, arcade, and rhythm box kits, chords the synths follow, parameter locks, ratchets, slides, swing, and sixteen punch-in effects. It is built on Felucca by way of X0X, AMB-1, and IND-1, installs from its own browser page, and can be tried first in a browser emulator.

entries.name: Mocky
entries.author: Charles Vestal
entries.what: A developer tool, not an instrument: it shows pictures sent from a web page on the FM1's screen, to check screen mockups on the real hardware, and can keep up to 64 in flash. It installs from its own browser page.
entries.photoAlt: Mocky's welcome screen, which says to plug in USB and open its page in Chrome

entries.name: Modular-1
entries.author: WiggisModular
entries.what: A modular synth after the Nord Modular: its web app builds patches from modules, maps their parameters and the knobs through a matrix, and uploads them to the FM1, which steps through patches and modules and adds an arpeggiator with Euclidean rhythms and chaos. Version 1.0.3 plays four voices. It installs from its release package.

entries.name: NOCT
entries.author: Joolo09
entries.what: A permanent MIDI preset for the FM1 with FL Studio and Ableton Live scripts, drawn as an animated night city with six scenes for chords, composing, rhythm, arpeggios, and sync. Its README, in Russian, is on version 0.9.4, and it installs from its own page with a browser emulator.

entries.name: picovave
entries.author: acidsound
entries.what: Firmware that runs PICO-8 carts (through the femto8 engine) on the FM1 and the SMK-37 Pro, with the controls mapped to the game pad. It installs from the picovave-fm1.fwsc package in its release, and carts are uploaded over SysEx. Its README is mostly about the SMK-37 Pro and does not state whether it has been tried on an FM1.

entries.name: ReVo
entries.author: gggguto
entries.what: An experimental soundscape instrument with two machines: Bioma, a synthesised ecosystem of birds, insects and water, and Atolls, two sample loops you steer with windows, fragments and landing points. A browser editor writes samples to its four device slots. Built on Felucca and SLOOP. It installs from its own browser page, which checks the package’s identity and hash.

entries.name: Synthesthetic
entries.author: michaeljsmalley
entries.what: An audio-visual instrument with 30 audio-reactive visualisers on the FM1's screen and over USB as a webcam. Its release notes say 0.2 has been tested on one FM1, with macOS only. It installs from its own browser page, and a browser version plays it first.

entries.name: TheReFmB1rth
entries.author: AlexanderSeel
entries.what: A four-machine acid groovebox: two 303-style mono synths, an 808, and a 909, with patterns, song chaining, and performance effects. Its notes record test passes on an FM1, and it has no licence file. It installs from its release package.

entries.name: RHYTM-SEC-1
entries.author: James Hampshire
entries.what: Expressive rhythm section ideas fast. Pick one of 19 styles and it draws patterns from that genre's feel, which keep evolving as you play, over a bass line in your key. Breaks, builds and fills on a button, a DJ filter, MIDI clock sync and USB audio stems for your DAW.
entries.photoAlt: House playing: the step grid, with the HOME page

entries.name: TRAPSTATION OS
entries.author: Schlensog Audio Lab
entries.what: A trap and phonk groovebox: six tracks with 808s, FM keys, bells and pads, generators for drums, hats, chords and bass, a sampler with slices, a piano roll, a live performance page with mutes, effect throws and bar jumps, and tape, VHS and vinyl colour on the master.
entries.photoAlt: TRAPSTATION OS

entries.name: COQUÍ
entries.author: saulofilho
entries.what: Latin and Caribbean groovebox: synthesized congas, bongos, timbales, guiro and cowbell, 14 grooves from salsa and bomba to dembow, tumbao and montuno lines over the chord you hold, generative parts in the clave, and effect scenes from a backyard to a dub.
entries.photoAlt: COQUÍ's boot screen: the coquí sings under the moon

entries.name: Wanderer
entries.author: Nicholas James / Low Vision Music
entries.what: Wanderer 1.4: author-tested synth for low-vision musicians. Protect an Anchor, evolve two layers, play 100 sounds, eight Scatter modes and a 13-pattern arp. Adaptive/steady Zoom, clear knob controls, adjustable display hold and optional audio cues.
entries.photoAlt: Wanderer Home screen with the protected Anchor, evolving memory and layer controls

entries.name: fm1-amy
entries.author: Dan Ellis
entries.what: A six-voice analog-style synth: AMY's emulations of the 128 Juno-60 factory patches, shaped with the AMYboard editor's patch knobs (oscillators, LFO, filter, envelopes, EQ, chorus, reverb, distortion) on eleven colour-coded pages. Plays over USB MIDI, and the AMYboard editor can edit it live.
entries.photoAlt: fm1-amy on an M-VAVE FM-1, showing the ENV page of patch A12 Brass Swell

entries.name: RAMBEAVER
entries.author: Trust This Mechanism
entries.what: A side-scrolling action game with synthesized music, sound effects and character voices. Defend the dam, ride through robot city, fly to the data center and stop Mother.

entries.name: ARP WAV 09
entries.author: Wav.09.02
entries.what: Minimalist, instinctive FirmWare: no menu, no sound presets, everything is played with the knobs. Six voices to play alone or chain together: ARP, WAV drone, SEQ, KIT drums, X02 ghost and alien noises, A09 ghost radio.
entries.photoAlt: Dinghy's screen: the name, the note played, a keyboard with the keys that sound

entries.name: BOP-1
entries.author: devrvega
entries.what: A music toy for children that is also a real synthesizer: every control is a friend whose body is the sound, and the same toy grows from pressing things at three, to beats and loops, to a subtractive synth with its real names. It installs from its own browser page, with an emulator to try first and printable guides.

entries.name: Crepuscular Homunculus
entries.author: TerkWerX
entries.what: A synth and four-track groovebox, called TERKINSTEIN until 0.26. It plays, edits, sequences, and saves on the FM1 itself, with piano-roll editing, saved song swing, and a virtual FM1 to try in a browser. It installs from its release package.

entries.name: CYMA-1
entries.author: TEG-Lizard-Man
entries.what: A playable Chladni plate: keys strike, bow or rain on a virtual metal plate, and the sand on the screen settles into the figure you hear, using modal synthesis. It installs from its release package (cyma-1-v1.1.3.fwsc). The README says it has run on a real FM1 since 2026-10-29.

entries.name: Doom FM-1 / SMK
entries.author: ChanceTheMaker
entries.what: A Doom-engine port for the FM-1 and the SMK-37 Pro and Elite, with the nine original maps and three weapons. Its page builds the right firmware for your model and installs it over USB from a browser, and can play it there first. It replaces the synth application, and its page says to back up your projects first. Release 26 for the FM-1 moves the controls to the GameDude layout; the SMK-37 build stays on release 24.

entries.name: FM-1 Doom
entries.author: zvenson
entries.what: Doom on the FM1, by sloopDX's author: one arena from the free FreeDM, played on the keys and knob with the FM1's screen as the display and synthesised sound effects, but no music. It installs from its own browser page, which can put sloopDX back, and keeps sloopDX's USB rescue. It needs no game data of your own.

entries.name: FMDj
entries.author: DEADACTIVE
entries.what: Game Boy music programs on the FM-1: LSDj, the tracker, and DMGo!, the drum machine, in a Game Boy emulator on its screen, keys and knobs. Bring your own ROM: the install page puts it in, in your browser.
entries.photoAlt: FMDj for the M-VAVE FM-1: its screen

entries.name: GameDude
entries.author: ChanceTheMaker
entries.what: A Game Boy emulator by Doom FM-1 / SMK’s maker. Its browser page installs it on an FM1 or an SMK-37, plays Game Boy cartridges in a simulator, and sends them to a game library on the device over USB or Bluetooth.

entries.name: Mighty Arp
entries.author: Moby Pixel
entries.what: Mighty Arp, from the creator of Mighty Synth Sampler, is a 4-op FM/subtractive synth built around a chance arpeggiator. Just hold a chord and let chance play the melody. 50 sounds plus a RANDOM mode that invents new ones, a 32-step sequencer, chords, effects and more.
entries.photoAlt: Mighty Arp's screen: HOME

entries.name: NU//METAL SKRATCHMASTER PRO
entries.author: mhellar
entries.what: A robot turntablist with a nu metal band: the speech synthesiser SAM says 27 words onto a virtual record that you scratch with the keys and jog wheel, over drop-tuned guitars, a bass, and a 12-piece kit locked to ten grooves. Its README says it runs on the FM1, and it installs from its own browser page.

entries.name: OCA-1
entries.author: charlesvestal
entries.what: An ocarina for the FM1, for games that listen, such as Ocarina of Time on a Switch 2. It installs from the signed release package, and its website has the manual.

entries.name: Quantum GammaWave
entries.author: Guille Lauría
entries.what: A six-track groovebox for the M-VAVE FM-1: nine engines and 273 sounds (analog, six-operator FM, wavetable, digital drums), a 64-step sequencer with probability and ratchets, song mode, scales and chords, a mod matrix and three FX buses, plus a browser emulator and a web editor.
entries.photoAlt: Quantum GammaWave banner

entries.name: Switch Blade
entries.author: OllieNicklinUK
entries.what: Four synth machines on Felucca, one per track with eight voices shared: OB-Z, a brassy poly; WAVE, from Void Wave; NANO, a 303 and a polysynth; and JUNO, with a Juno-60-style chorus. It has no drums, as a synth expansion played over MIDI, and installs from its own page.

entries.name: THEORY-1
entries.author: wave00066
entries.what: Lessons, quizzes, and a chord lab for music theory, from scales and modes to chords and keys, in English, Italian, Spanish, and German. It installs from its release package, and its README says it is not yet tested on every unit.

entries.name: TONIC
entries.author: RahelPuest
entries.what: A Digitone-style FM groovebox with four-operator FM, virtual analogue, and drum engines, twelve voices, and a 64-step sequencer with parameter locks. Its README says it runs on an FM1, though its 0.12 release notes say it has not yet been tested on a physical one. It installs from its own browser page, with an emulator to try first.

entries.name: RAKT
entries.author: Chase DeAnda
entries.what: Pick a style and generate a band in one press. Chords, bass, drums and melody stay in sync and play off each other. In GLO Live, use the keys to solo parts, cue fills and drops, and play effects over the groove.
entries.photoAlt: Twelve RAKT FM-1 screens showing Song, musician panels, Mix, Saved Takes, Help, Generator, ARP, FX Space and Sound Library

entries.name: glitch
entries.author: saulofilho
entries.what: Neon-noir groovebox firmware for the M-VAVE FM-1: four tracks, seven sources, tape and megacity space FX, sixteen scales (Insen, Hirajoshi, Iwato, whole tone), and forty-four Blade Runner factory sounds. Its screen: a glitched landscape that tears with the sound.
entries.photoAlt: The GL!TCH hub: the glitched landscape, alive, and the name standing on its plain

entries.name: M-Vance
entries.author: Kris (bk40-home)
entries.what: A JP-8000/8080-style virtual analog on eight voices: the JT-8000 engine ported to the FM-1, with Super Saw, the JP filter, multi-effects, delay, a plate reverb, an arpeggiator and 64 programs, every knob on the JP-8080's own MIDI CCs.
entries.photoAlt: The M-vance home screen: the name, the program, the note, a keyboard with the keys that sound

entries.name: DUB-BOX
entries.author: altessproduction
entries.what: A dub station for the M-VAVE FM-1: the USB/BT audio router with sloop-DUB's dub modules on top — a dub siren, a tape echo, a bipolar DJ filter and a four-band isolator, each page's four settings on K1-K4, the black keys as the live performance: the eighth turns the dub on and off, the ninth and…
entries.photoAlt: DUB-BOX

entries.name: CORD
entries.author: Chase DeAnda
entries.what: Pick a chord progression, press Play, and play along with drums, bass and chords. Adjust the progression, sounds and groove to build backing tracks for practicing, jamming and writing songs.
entries.photoAlt: Actual firmware playback: Devil in Ember and Cat in Plum, with changing chords, phrase playheads and animated beat rings

entries.name: cursed os
entries.author: cursedsound
entries.what: An Elektron-style six-track groovebox for the FM-1, with Elektron Syntakt support. One-press quick-start loops, generators for acid lines, dub chords, held atmospheres and modular bleeps, trig conditions and locks, a DJ filter and FX pad, and the keys set the song's key. Built on JIANT FM.
entries.photoAlt: cursed os in the browser emulator

entries.name: Manta
entries.author: delirioux
entries.what: Generative Latin grooves for the FM-1: a band on the clave in twelve styles, from salsa and mambo to bolero, bossa and tango, with sampled percussion, upright piano, brass, sax, violins and double bass. Lead the band with hits and a mambo, take the trumpet solo on the keys, or play and edit each…
entries.photoAlt: The home screen's four scopes, PLAY, the instrument pages and an EDIT, from the firmware itself

entries.name: MORPHEUS
entries.author: Ben Badio
entries.what: A pattern sequencer after Reason's Matrix: up to four channels of MIDI sequence data out, and a few voices built in to build the patterns with.
entries.photoAlt: MORPHEUS 8-Track Groovebox Banner

entries.name: Tack
entries.author: oikoaudio
entries.what: A seven-voice drum synth on the LXR firmware's engine. Its step sequencer has per-lane length and direction. Steps have parameter locks, chance and pass conditions, so one pattern can change from pass to pass. It loads LXR-02 .SND kits, sends 10 channels of USB audio and syncs to MIDI clock.
entries.photoAlt: The Tack plugin's editor: a tab per voice, with boxes of dials for the oscillator, FM, transient, filter, envelopes, mix and LFO.

entries.name: Blues Box
entries.author: Brian Provost
entries.what: 12-bar and 8-bar blues & funk backing band (19 grooves, 14 bass engines, 18 keyboard tones, 12 drum kits) with independent Fullness & Variation controls, live cues, 16 white-key preset slots, and a 4-voice lead synth with scale LEDs & optional Easy Lead scale-bend mode.
entries.photoAlt: Lead Sheet

entries.name: BEETLE BLUE
entries.author: Joppe Sikken (SikkenWorks)
entries.what: BEETLE BLUE turns your M-VAVE FM1 into a six-lane drum tracker. Build beats with BEETLE and MONOLITH kits, design custom drums, arrange songs, and perform setlists with Live Mode and hands-on effects.
entries.photoAlt: BEETLE BLUE pixel-art boot image

entries.name: FM-1 SID
entries.author: Joakim Eriksson
entries.what: C64 music on the FM-1: a 6510 runs each tune's own code and reSID plays it, PSID and RSID. A GoatTracker 2 editor on the FM-1 itself with ten GT2 example songs, a SID synth with a sequencer and effects, and any .sid sent from the browser plays at once.
entries.photoAlt: The emulated FM-1's front panel running fifteen of the firmwares in turn

entries.name: Monohull
entries.author: Mark White
entries.what: A monosynth: one voice with analogue-modelled oscillators and five filters (ladder, diode ladder, OTA, Sallen-Key, state-variable), unison, chorus, delay and reverb, and 14 presets.
entries.photoAlt: Monohull's screen

entries.name: AMB-1 Evolved
entries.author: kidbee85-beep
entries.what: A generative ambient firmware that keeps AMB-1’s controls, with 64 sounds and 32 themes. Its README, in German, says its maker tried release E1 on their FM1 on 17 October. It installs from its own browser page.

entries.name: BAILE
entries.author: arrastao
entries.what: Brazilian rhythm kits by Mulú: Tamborzão, Voltmix, and Beat Bolha, with 12 samples built in and a 16-step bar for each preset. Its README calls 0.7 stable after a user reported it working on their FM1. It installs from its release package.

entries.name: Boardwalk
entries.author: charlesvestal
entries.what: A seaside arcade of music games for the FM1: cabinets such as Striker, Moles, Tiles, Gull and Teacups pay out tickets that trade for prizes. It installs from its own browser page or from its release package, and can be tried in a browser emulator first. The README does not say whether it has been tried on an FM1.

entries.name: BRUTAL FM
entries.author: hiroikezawa
entries.what: An FM synth for industrial techno, noise, and dark ambient, built on Felucca: four operators in a 4×4 modulation matrix, METAL, GROWL, CHAOS, and NOISE modes, a wavefolder, a morph between two sounds, and a COMPLEX ARP that generates a pattern from the keys held and keeps it as a loop. Its README, in Japanese, says it runs on an FM1. It installs from its release package.

entries.name: DIRGE
entries.author: sinscum
entries.what: Darksynth, noise, and drone firmware built on Felucca 1.6.1: four tracks, fifteen engines among them its own DRONE and BASS, a 64-step sequencer per track with chords, ratchets, conditions, and parameter locks, an arpeggiator, a song chain, and MIDI clock in, under long, worn effects. It installs from its own browser page, plays the real firmware in a browser, and has a web editor for sounds, samples, and backups.

entries.name: Doom (E1M1)
entries.author: seanohollaren
entries.what: Doom as the FM1's firmware, separate from FM-1 Doom. It has been installed and played on one FM1, replaces the synth firmware, and installs from its own browser page, which fetches the shareware game data into your browser.

entries.name: Double Rainbow
entries.author: joshbartlettband-web
entries.what: Rainbow mode's older sibling, for ages ten and up, built on Melodee: 30 characters escaped from the Keeper's jars, each a real synth engine, from a Prophet-5 and FM to a TB-303 and an 808. Each has four knobs, a beat, an arp, and codex pages on its engine, with chord modes, an ear trainer, and 14 songs to learn one key at a time. Holding HOME and SAVE opens the full Melodee synth. It installs from its own browser page, and plays in a browser first.
entries.photoAlt: Double Rainbow's Vesper, a moth in a velvet cape, under a rainbow, with four knobs: GLOW, BITE, BLOOM and DRIFT

entries.name: Drumtonic
entries.author: Federico Ciapi
entries.what: A drum machine for the FM-1: ten synthesized drum channels, 32 patterns of up to 64 steps with p-locks, conditions, micro timing and ratchets, free recording with QUANT, beat repeat, 8 LFOs per pattern, reverb, tape delay and a master compressor. No samples, no computer needed.
entries.photoAlt: LIVE: the pattern, its kit, the channels' meters, tempo and swing on the knobs

entries.name: Emerald YM
entries.author: CaspiusLabs
entries.what: A generative 16-bit music firmware with a YM2612 FM sound, Sega-style PSG voices, live keys, and per-instrument effects. Its release notes call 1.0.4 a stable release, retested on an FM1, and it installs from its release package.

entries.name: FMLarynx
entries.author: Presethead
entries.what: A throaty talking formant synth with a 303-style sequencer: a saw wave through a three-formant vowel filter, resonant low-pass, drive and ping-pong delay. 16 steps with vowels, accent and slide, a pattern randomizer, 16 stored patterns, Bluetooth MIDI and tight clock sync.
entries.photoAlt: FMLarynx's screen: a throat whose opening follows the vowel, the note in it, the step strip and the keyboard

entries.name: Golf
entries.author: BARNIR
entries.what: A wavetable synthesizer: two oscillators that morph through 130 wavetables, with unison and warps, a ladder filter, a modulation matrix and effects. Its 32-step sequencer can move the wavetable and the filter on every step.
entries.photoAlt: Golf on the FM-1's screen

entries.name: LSDJ Burrito
entries.author: Dreamy_bacon
entries.what: Little Sound Dj, the Game Boy tracker, on the FM-1: played from its keys and knobs, with per-channel filters, drive, lo-fi and an LFO, a shared echo, reverb and compressor, MIDI sync and colour themes. Bring your own LSDj: the project's web page adds it to this firmware on your computer.
entries.photoAlt: The web page's Perform view: the FM-1 (here the virtual FM-1 running LSDj), the master effects, the four channel pages at once, and the wiring of every effect

entries.name: LUOGU
entries.author: Reytian
entries.what: Peking opera percussion and jinghu accompaniment: learn the percussion patterns by playing along, or sing an aria with its own band. Its README says it runs on an FM1, though most of its testing has been in a simulator. It installs from its release package.

entries.name: Miku-FM
entries.author: Michael Perry
entries.what: A singing songwriter: a pixel singer sings your songs in Japanese, consonants and all, over FM chords, bass and drums. Shape her voice with effects, harmony and five characters, write patterns or let her generate a whole song, and watch her dance. 8 song slots.
entries.photoAlt: Miku-FM's Stage screen: a pixel-art Hatsune Miku with the syllable dial below her

entries.name: Moondaw
entries.author: jaeggerr
entries.what: A tracker with eight tracks, instruments you build yourself, three effects a step, and songs kept as plain text files that an LLM can write. Its README calls it a beta tried on a real FM1 every day, and it installs from its own browser page, plays in a browser, and has a manual.

entries.name: NAIWAN 91
entries.author: superposition
entries.what: City pop and coastal firmware: nineteen genres, ten urban and nine coastal, that play themselves while you steer, each with ten jam pieces on the firmware’s own FM, analogue and percussion engines. It installs from its own browser page, which also plays it in an emulator.

entries.name: Norilsk
entries.author: nzimas
entries.what: A firmware for inhospitable soundscapes: three generators drawn at random, three effect slots to wreck them, and a master delay and plate reverb. Its README calls it for ambient hellscapes and barren atmospheres, and it installs from its own browser page.

entries.name: OPX
entries.author: thomasgregorymarsden-code
entries.what: Felucca 1.5.1 with one more engine, an altered-FM engine after the Korg opsix: six operators routed by an algorithm, EGs, LFOs, a filter, and effects. Everything Felucca does stays. A project with an OPX track opens only on OPX. It has a browser simulator and an editor with an OPX tab, and installs from its own page, which can return the FM1 to M-VAVE’s V15.

entries.name: OPX Solo
entries.author: thomasgregorymarsden-code
entries.what: The OPX firmware with the OPX engine alone: one part, with the memory of all four parts, so every opsix effect type fits and the short delay reaches 300 ms. Other tracks of a project stay in it but are silent. It has its own browser simulator and editor, and installs from its own page.

entries.name: Pink Trombone
entries.author: stefanolofsson
entries.what: A voice synthesiser built on the Pink Trombone vocal tract model, as fm1-dock with the trombone as its only synth, so USB, the installers and the rescue keep working. It installs from the pinktrombone-0.1.fwsc package in its release.

entries.name: Quasar
entries.author: nzimas
entries.what: Firmware after SOMA Laboratory’s Pulsar-23, for experimental IDM, with an audio engine written from scratch: six tracks, 16 engine profiles, 147 sound families, macros, a phrase generator with polymeters, and a performance mode. It installs from its own browser page, which its README says to open in desktop Chrome, Edge, or Opera, and the site carries a manual.

entries.name: SHIFL
entries.author: schwartzworld
entries.what: A live groovebox firmware based on Felucca, with six synth tracks and a drum machine, a song mode, USB audio, MIDI clock and a full backup. It installs from its own browser page, which also has an editor and a way back to the official firmware. Its README calls it a beta and says to install at your own risk. It has no GitHub releases.

entries.name: M-Vsynth2
entries.author: Kris (bk40-home)
entries.what: Synth2, the open-source recreation of Synth1, on eight voices across both cores: two oscillators and a sub, five filters (LPDL among them), two LFOs, distortions and phasers, EQ, delay, chorus and Synth1's arpeggiator. It plays Synth1's .sy1 patches, with the Synth2 Factory bank built in and 1024…

entries.name: Quartet
entries.author: MammothCheese
entries.what: A four-track groovebox that plays like a four-piece band: lead, pads, bass and drums. 40 sounds and 10 drum kits, 5 effect pedals, an arpeggiator, step and live recording, and a song sequencer where each instrument follows its own arrangement.
entries.photoAlt: QUARTET's screens: home, the sound browser, the signal chain, a pedal, the step recorder, the drum grid, the mixer, SUPER SEQ

entries.name: Piterfly
entries.author: Piotr Woźniak
entries.what: A groovebox OS for M-VAVE FM-1, built on SLOOP and Felucca: six synths plus two independent drum tracks, 24 patterns, 128 SONG positions and up to eight named songs in 352 KiB shared storage. Save/load from a list, delete and export songs to a computer. FUNB projects require new work; user-sample…
entries.photoAlt: piterfly

entries.name: SPLITMILK
entries.author: MammothCheese
entries.what: SPLITMILK is a performance-focused firmware that separates the keyboard into two independent instruments, with chords, arpeggiators, effects and an adjustable split. Play both instruments live over built-in drum and pad sequencers to create music without endless menu-diving.
entries.photoAlt: SPLITMILK's main screen: CHOC and BERRY side by side

entries.name: Pocket Band
entries.author: elpabl0
entries.what: A band in your FM-1. Pick a spot on a map of 16 genre towns and it writes a four-piece sketch: drums, bass, keys and lead in one key. Re-roll parts, audition players, jam, morph, play punch-in effects, edit steps, save four slots. With a rhythm game played over your own drum part.
entries.photoAlt: Three Pocket Band screens: the map, the stage and the run

entries.name: Sardine
entries.author: delirioux
entries.what: Live club mixing for the FM-1: four layers (lead, chord, bass, drums) that play by themselves in 20 styles while you ride them live. Blend one style into the next, build with intros and break-build-drop arcs, edit steps or play a layer by hand. All synthesised but the piano.
entries.photoAlt: MAIN, playing

entries.name: EVIL GENIUS
entries.author: Quixotic7
entries.what: A SID chip groovebox that talks. Six tracks of C64 SID voices and SAM speech, per-step sound locks, conditions, ratchets and MIDI FX, and a tower of eight retro effects with a send per track. Bluetooth MIDI and USB audio. A C64 game for a screen.
entries.photoAlt: The title screen

entries.name: keySTEP ONE
entries.author: dzwerg
entries.what: A four-track MIDI arranger and controller for the M-VAVE FM-1. Create patterns, songs and albums, switch patterns live, route USB and Bluetooth MIDI, and play sounds with the onboard General MIDI synth.
entries.photoAlt: keySTEP ONE for the M-VAVE FM-1: its screen

entries.name: Stallion
entries.author: Eberon Limited (John Gorman)
entries.what: A synthesizer with 26 engines and 819 level-matched factory sounds: three-oscillator HYBRID, six-operator FM, wavetables, early-1980s polysynths, a semi-modular two-filter voice, physical models and more. One instrument with a modulation matrix, arpeggiator and step sequencer, edited in the browser.

entries.name: Hungry Travis
entries.author: Trust This Mechanism
entries.what: A spoon-feeding balance game with a beatless ambient soundtrack and voiced reactions. Balance a bean, guide the spoon and try to feed Travis. Every fifth bite sets off a transformation.

entries.name: CONDUCTOR
entries.author: MammothCheese
entries.what: A pocket symphony orchestra groovebox with strings, woodwinds, brass and percussion. Compose in piano roll or musical notation, conduct individual sections with articulations, dynamics and expression curves, and arrange patterns into complete pieces.
entries.photoAlt: The orchestra page

entries.name: Kurzhaar, der Basshund
entries.author: JazzMasterT
entries.what: A monophonic analog-style bass synth with a step sequencer: two oscillators and a sub into a resonant ladder filter, two LFOs, drive and reverb, 16 presets. Basslines in your key and scale, 16 patterns, tight sync to a DAW's MIDI clock, and recording over USB audio.
entries.photoAlt: Kurzhaar, der Basshund

entries.name: PLAYA
entries.author: JFS
entries.what: A performance firmware built on Optimist: two synth layers on one keyboard (layer, split, blend or single), drums with a simple step sequencer, send effects, Bluetooth MIDI keyboards, and one easy to read screen with knobs 1-4 to edit all parameters. 5 engines, 32 drum kits, 135 presets.
entries.photoAlt: The FM-1's screen: the mixer with the tracks T1 to T3 and the drum track playing

entries.name: Tekstuur
entries.author: BARNIR
entries.what: An instrument for slow, evolving sound. Four layers play recorded sources as drifting loops, grains, time-stretch or resonating strings, mixed by a vector point that moves by itself, with shimmer reverb and freeze.
entries.photoAlt: Tekstuur on the FM-1's screen

entries.name: Album
entries.author: joshbartlettband-web
entries.what: A series of firmwares, one per record, by Rainbow mode's maker: a few deep sounds drawn from photographs, each moving its photo as it plays. Album 01 bends chords the whole time they ring, through a reverse reverb, with a chord on every key, a soft beat for every patch, and two FM1s playing together over MIDI clock. It installs from its own browser page, and plays in a browser first.

entries.name: AmbWave
entries.author: mentalcells
entries.what: An ambient instrument built on Felucca: four tracks of curated sounds, held chords, scattered notes, and four knobs for Shape, Motion, Density, and Space. It installs from its own web page, with a browser version to try first.

entries.name: ANDROMEDA
entries.author: Polaris Sound Lab
entries.what: An ambient instrument. ALIGN writes a whole 4-track piece in one of 13 moods, always in key; AUTO keeps it growing from your own pattern. SKY macros, a three-head SPACE TAPE echo with spring, and visions drawn from the music: cymatics, harmonograph, attractor and orrery.
entries.photoAlt: ANDROMEDA on the FM-1: ALIGN, AUTO, KEYS, SKY, SPACE TAPE, VISION

entries.name: ASS-ID
entries.author: altessproduction
entries.what: The ATEK303 acid groovebox plus a drum track on the same clock: eight synthesized TR-808/909/707 voices, no samples, a seeded 64-step generator with mutations and LOCK for both tracks, an 8x16 drum matrix, swing, three kits, drive, chorus, delay, reverb and eight factory presets.
entries.photoAlt: DVOX

entries.name: Bass Something 2
entries.author: imijes
entries.what: A monosynth firmware in the style of the Bass Station 2, with 32 factory patches of its own and Bass Station II patch dumps in and out over SysEx. It also works from an iPhone or iPad in RemoteFM1, and from 0.8.1 plays through Bluetooth headphones and speakers. It installs from its own browser page, which also plays it in an emulator, and has a manual.

entries.name: Bongo Cat’s Tiny Studio
entries.author: ImpossibleKnot
entries.what: A playable little band built on Felucca 1.6.1: a cat plays the keys while three more react to the music, with thirteen sound engines, a generated backing band, and a looper for your own melodies. Its README says the upgrade from 0.3.0 to this release candidate was tested on one FM1. It installs through Felucca's updater from its release package.

entries.name: BoopBox
entries.author: Josh-McFarlin
entries.what: A renamed fork of SLOOP that carries on from SLOOP 2.8.3 with an eight-track project format of its own. Since 14 Nov its site, installer, and web editor are on Replit. It installs from its own browser page, which also updates an FM1 running SLOOP or Felucca, and has a web editor.

entries.name: Braindancer
entries.author: NorfolkHacker
entries.what: An IDM and braindance firmware, a fork of JIANT FM, formerly called ACID FM. Its 0.9.1, the version its README names, trims JIANT's engines for IDM, gives its sound, sequencer, global and MIDI screens an acid look of its own, and has a generator that writes whole songs on the device across its genres; breakbeats loaded from its web page are planned. It installs from its own browser page, which also plays it in an emulator, and has a manual.

entries.name: CORTEX
entries.author: guiatihe333
entries.what: A generative FM instrument forked from AMB-1: three six-operator FM voices with DX7 banks play chords that grow by themselves, a tape reel records and replays them, songs come in from MIDI files, and a video synth on the screen moves with the music, while a cartoon cat explains each page. It installs from the.fwsc package on its release page and plays in a browser simulator first.

entries.name: DABKE
entries.author: STUDIOMORPHIK
entries.what: An Arabic wedding keyboard. Maqam scales with quarter tones on any note, dabke and shaabi rhythms, mijwiz, zurna, oud and qanun voices, a drone, eight tracks with loops and steps. Lean on a key and the note bends. An Akai MIDImix works as its mixer.
entries.photoAlt: DABKE's home screen: the singer on his stage

entries.name: FIELD
entries.author: AveyCole
entries.what: A field-recording radio powered by Radio Aporee, over the FM1's Wi-Fi: choose a country or region on a globe and listen, then capture a few seconds into a lo-fi sampler that plays on the keys, loops, and slices. Its README says the first alpha was reported working on an FM1, and that 0.1.19, which its installer page offers, still needs a test on one.

entries.name: FM-1 Ear Trainer
entries.author: copych
entries.what: An ear-training game on Melodee: it plays one to four hidden notes in C major or A minor, in one octave or across the keyboard, and you find them on the keys, with current and best ratings saved for each mode and FM6 or Prophet sounds. It installs from its own browser page, which also plays it in an emulator, and has a guide.

entries.name: FM-1 Midi-Mania
entries.author: Shan-Sherif
entries.what: A rhythm game for the FM-1. Load songs from the browser Studio, turn any MIDI file into a song: your part's notes fall to the keys and you play KEYS, DRUMS, GUITAR or BASS while the FM-1 plays the rest on its synth engines. Every note judged, with combos and best scores.
entries.photoAlt: FM-1 Midi-Mania played on an FM-1: notes fall on its screen while the keys are played

entries.name: fm1-wheel
entries.author: ograndebe
entries.what: A tonewheel organ after setBfree, with drawbars, percussion, a Leslie with slow, fast and stop rotor, drive and reverb, on fm1-base and felucca-bsp. Its README says the FM1 build has been flashed and tested on a real FM1 (8 Nov), and that its SMK-37 Pro build passes its host tests but has not been flashed yet. It installs from its own page, which carries both builds.

entries.name: FM1_AudioBase
entries.author: stevexfer
entries.what: The FM1 as a USB audio interface and nothing more: what the computer plays reaches the FM1's outputs, MASTER sets the volume, and GLO shows a visualiser, and it is meant as a small base to start new firmware from. Its README says both USB audio streams, MASTER, and the visualiser were tested on an FM1, and calls it very early development. It installs from its own browser page.

entries.name: FMtribe
entries.author: GuinanNo1
entries.what: A firmware after the Korg monotribe: one oscillator, a two-pole filter, an LFO, three drums and an eight-step sequencer, written without Korg code. So far it is an early test build that plays fm1-base’s test voice under its name; the instrument itself comes next. It installs from its own browser page, which also has an emulator, a quickstart and a manual.

entries.name: FN ACID
entries.author: Electro-Dig
entries.what: A firmware where every track is a function drawn on one pair of axes and played as it is drawn. Its ACID track plays sixteen steps you write, the 303's way, or a formula, through a ping-pong delay and a small room, with punch-in effects. It is built on Dinghy, SLOOP, and Felucca, comes as numbered test builds, and installs from its own web page.

entries.name: FORMALFRED
entries.author: mpancia
entries.what: A generative sequencer of four lanes whose sequencing logic is proved in Lean 4, made at a hackathon. Its site has a web installer and a browser simulator, its licence is GPL-3.0, and its README does not say it has been heard on an FM1.

entries.name: GabberBuddy
entries.author: gybe808-dotcom
entries.what: A firmware based on Felucca and XOX. It installs from its web installer, in Chrome or Edge, which also has a Back to the stock firmware button.

entries.name: GIO-1
entries.author: GuinanNo1
entries.what: A generative disco machine in the style of Giorgio Moroder: it plays itself from power-on with bass, strings, a lead and drums, across nine song presets you steer by key, pattern and section. It installs from its release package and plays in a browser emulator first. Its 0.3.1-beta notes call it beta, installed on three FM1s so far with no major issues reported, and still advise installing with caution.

entries.name: Haunted FM1
entries.author: davidpryan
entries.what: Five generative firmwares for haunted ambient music with meaningful controls: Halflight, Midnight, Untrue, Voicemail, and Worntape. Its flasher page installs any of them from Chrome or Edge, and the release carries a package for each.

entries.name: IND-1
entries.author: devrvega
entries.what: A self-playing industrial machine after the records of KMFDM, Nine Inch Nails, and Ministry: it starts as soon as it is switched on and arranges its own songs, with song and drum editors. It installs from its own browser page.

entries.name: KIDBOY
entries.author: WillCMcC
entries.what: A toy for toddlers: the keys play nursery songs, say and show letters, count, or play their own notes, the buttons are drums, and there are no menus. It comes as a release package.

entries.name: Kris Jangle
entries.author: w33tSnx
entries.what: Kris Jangle is a Christmas game for the FM-1: it plays the start of a carol and you replay it on the keys, building three notes per level up to the whole song. Four carols, three play modes from guided EASY to sound-only HARD, and Grump Mode on three misses.
entries.photoAlt: Kris Jangle title screen

entries.name: LVM Wanderer
entries.author: spinnicholas
entries.what: An experimental event-memory synth designed for low-vision musicians, with large high-contrast symbols, a protected Anchor idea that evolves into phrases, 100 presets and chorus, delay and reverb. It installs from the.fwsc package in its release. Its release says the author confirmed this build on a physical FM1 on 2 November.

entries.name: Mini-Ju08
entries.author: Stephane Schmitz
entries.what: A Jupiter-8 style synthesizer for the M-VAVE FM-1 (both hardware versions). Eight voices in two parts (Whole, Dual, Split or 2-Part), two VCOs per voice with sync and cross mod, HPF and 12/24 dB ladder VCF, two ADSRs, LFO, arpeggiator and polyphonic portamento, 64 patches. Chorus and 17 MFX types…

entries.name: Mini-Vision
entries.author: eldontyrellcorp
entries.what: A wavetable synthesiser after Roland's n/vision, forked from Mini-Tone. Two wavetable layers with 63 tables, a sine-fold wave shaper, phase modulation, and a choice of filters, with the interface drawn after the n/vision's. It keeps Mini-Tone's TR-808 engine and installs from its release package.

entries.name: NIGHTFALL
entries.author: SylarPu-X
entries.what: A cyberpunk-inspired performance synth with a sequencer, effects, and a browser studio. Its README says the package has booted on one FM1 and passed its protocol tests there. It installs from its own browser updater.

entries.name: OPLBend Tracker
entries.author: AudrenThibault
entries.what: An LSDJ-style tracker on an OPL3-style FM engine, with 18 voices, effects inspired by circuit bending, a drum machine and a looper. It opens and exports AdLib Tracker II songs, and also runs on a Mac as a VST3 plugin. It installs from its own browser page.

entries.name: OPLBOX
entries.author: LXXero
entries.what: The FM1 as an AdLib: an OPL2 emulation that plays SoundFX Macs Opera songs, the DOS soundtracks of LINEL’s games and Stone Age, and since 0.4 a tracker that edits and saves them as.CMF files. Its README says earlier versions ran on a real FM1. It installs from its release package.

entries.name: RED MASS VAMPIRE OS
entries.author: karlalex732-dotcom
entries.what: Six tracks, five instruments and drums, with 256 built-in sounds, two trap kits, 64 steps a track, and a song mode. Its release carries a firmware package and a Windows installer, and its README says booting and running it on an FM1 still need checking.

entries.name: ReplicantFM1
entries.author: DanimanX
entries.what: An acid, techno and big-beat groovebox forked from Felucca, with a drum machine modelled on the TR-909, a mono synth modelled on the SH-101, two TB-303-style basslines with an algorithmic generator, and a sliced breakbeat player that takes your own loops. It installs from its own browser page, which can also put M-VAVE’s firmware back, and has a manual.

entries.name: SARDAB
entries.author: jrdntnnr
entries.what: A dungeon-synth firmware turned toward the desert, built on GHOULBOX (a Felucca fork) with maqam tuning, Arabic rhythms, oud and ney recordings and stone-room reverbs. It installs from its own browser page. The README calls the current build a development preview that has been tested on a host and emulator, with validation on a physical FM1 still pending.

entries.name: SEQ-4
entries.author: devrvega
entries.what: Turns the FM-1 into four MIDI sequencers (melody, chords, eight-track drums and two generative modes) for controlling other instruments; the FM-1 makes no sound of its own. The README calls it young (0.x) and reports timing measured on an FM-1. It installs from its own browser page in Chrome or Edge, and also from its release package, with a browser emulator to try first.

entries.name: SPIRALFM1
entries.author: Spiralfractalplugins
entries.what: A four-track live groovebox built on Mycelium and SLOOP, with six psytrance, techno, and acid grooves, four 240-bar factory songs, a PSY FX page, and per-track probability. It installs from its own browser page.

entries.name: Stack Trace CFW
entries.author: jonludwig1234
entries.what: A firmware built on M-VAVE’s FM1 Open V14 that adds four engines, a virtual analogue polysynth, a TR-909, a C64 SID, and a granular one, with a 128-step sequencer with Euclidean and 303 acid generators, an eight-scene clip launcher, grit and punch effects, a sample slicer, MIDI CC learn, and four demo songs. It installs from its release package with M-VAVE’s FM-1 Workbench.

entries.name: Tidepool
entries.author: pjh-133
entries.what: An ambient loop instrument with twelve synthesised scenes that play by themselves, and a Blank Canvas for recording your own loops. It installs from its own browser page and can be tried first in a browser.

entries.name: Typhoon
entries.author: ignis32
entries.what: A firmware for playing the FM1 from an EWI wind controller, with a preset editor and a simulator in the browser. Its README calls it an early alpha whose controls are still changing, and it installs from its own browser page.

entries.name: VIRGO
entries.author: mongio
entries.what: A gravitational-wave synthesiser by Mario Texture, sister of Grana: every note is a black-hole merger, with four events at once, a detector you tune like a radio, and a long reverb with shimmer. It installs through an editor page in its release, which also simulates it, and has a Bluetooth variant. Its interface is in Italian.

entries.name: X0X Extended Edition
entries.author: Acultur8
entries.what: A fork of X0X that keeps its 909, 808, two 303s, and breakbeat player and adds song blocks and variations, per-sound filters and limiters, and finer timing divisions. Sequences copy whole or one part at a time, any single drum row or either 303, keeping the destination's accents and swing, and each paste can be undone. Tested on only one FM1 so far.

entries.name: AETHER FM1
entries.author: GR!MM
entries.what: Dark ambient, dungeon synth and deathdream firmware: 4 tracks, 7 sound sources, real recorded choirs, tracks that play by themselves, and long tape, granular and reverb effects.
entries.photoAlt: GR!MM on the FM-1: the HOME screen

entries.name: FMav-1
entries.author: wootrop & gpix
entries.what: A semi-modular mono synth calibrated knob by knob on a real one: VCO, self-oscillating 4-pole ladder filter, LFO, ADSR, VCA, wave folder, S+H, mixer and a patchbay with normals and dummy plugs. Four tracks, MIDI clock sync, chorus, delay and reverb, 90 sounds.

entries.name: Golana DZ Edition
entries.author: dzwerg
entries.what: Golana's synth with a sequencer for whole songs: 64 steps a pattern, 32 programs (up to 2,048 steps), a SONGMODE that plays from a first to a last program once or on repeat, and USB MIDI out to sequence other synths.
entries.photoAlt: Golana DZ Edition for the M-VAVE FM-1: its screen

entries.name: Astra
entries.author: Michael Perry
entries.what: Your birth chart as an FM synth: the FM-1 works out the planets itself, casts your chart, and the aspects between today's sky and your chart wire ten FM operators, one per planet. Four voices, a horoscope you can read on the screen, a sky you can run at five years a second, chorus, echo, reverb…

entries.name: Mini-Grain
entries.author: eldontyrellcorp
entries.what: A granular synth on your FM-1: two polyphonic granular parts plus a drone and a pad, each with a filter, two LFOs and its own step sequencer, into a shared ping-pong delay and plate reverb. Seven sample generators, your own samples sent over USB from a web page, 16 presets, and USB and TRS MIDI…

entries.name: XENOLITH
entries.author: Unit_v743
entries.what: An experimental mono-track FM cell synthesizer with programmable oscillator routing, modulation, sequencing, a vintage circuit-derived filter, VCA, wavefolding, digital fidelity reduction and reverb. A load engine models physical voltage sag and progressively shrinks resource usage under stress.
entries.photoAlt: Xenolith boot emblem

entries.name: Juicy
entries.author: Daniel Gilbert
entries.what: A groovebox for jamming, made easy to pick up: drums, bass, an arpeggiator that follows the pad's chords, a pad and a lead, in patterns and a chain. Pick a key and the keys light up what fits; grooves, chord progressions and a demo song get you started. Undo, live recording, a mixer per pattern.
entries.photoAlt: The JUICY screen of DEMO1: the chain of patterns, tempo, reverb, swing and key

entries.name: AISLING FX-1
entries.author: CU_STE
entries.what: Turns the FM-1 into an effects box. Sound from a computer, sent over USB, comes out of its socket through AISLING's live effects: reverb, shimmer, echo, phaser, drive, crush and more, held by key or CC. Knobs set the filter, sends and dry, and the wet sound goes back up the cable.
entries.photoAlt: AISLING FX-1: a gold 8-bit harp on green, with FX beside it

entries.name: QUARTZ
entries.author: f0nski
entries.what: A four-track groovebox: Plaits' 24 models, a 16-pad kit, a step sequencer with p-locks and trig conditions, eight generative sources (Game of Life, chord progressions, Tonnetz walks, orbits, an improviser that learns from you...), punch-in effects and an animated scene on every page.

entries.name: amb-pond
entries.author: superxor
entries.what: A generative garden pond. Switch it on and it plays itself: breathing voices, water drops, a gliding bass and quiet drips, with echo and reverb. Nine pieces, from a quiet pond to rain and thunder. Pick a piece and a scale, take notes out or put them back, and let it grow.
entries.photoAlt: The pond in daylight

entries.name: AQUORA
entries.author: CodingSlapfu
entries.what: A generative ambient firmware of Solfeggio tones, binaural beats, and soundscapes, with eight musical roles including drums, an eight-track console, and its own AQUORA Sans font. Its 0.7.14 release notes link the firmware package and say testing on a physical FM1 is still pending. Its README says the owner verified 0.2.0 playback on an FM1.

entries.name: ARPHONY
entries.author: ttreu
entries.what: A modal arpeggiator firmware that plays riffs over slowly moving modal chords, with a bass note and up to two chord tones. It is built on M-VAVE's FM1 Open. It installs from its own browser page or the release package. Its README says it was tested on one FM-1 unit; no licence is stated.

entries.name: Atl-Atl
entries.author: jasonbot
entries.what: A USB audio interface and autotuner on FM1_AudioBase: play computer audio into it and hold a key to tune it, with a three-second sampler, tempo, an arpeggiator mask, and latch. Its README says it has been installed and updated on a real FM1, and calls the autotuner a work in progress. It installs from its release package, and plays in a browser emulator.

entries.name: Atl-Atl: The Atltuner
entries.author: Jason Scheirer
entries.what: A USB audio interface and autotuner for the M-VAVE FM-1. Play computer audio into it, hold a key to tune it, and use the three-second sampler, tempo, ARP mask and latch.
entries.photoAlt: Atl-Atl screen: selected note C4, sample, modes, BPM and settings

entries.name: BB1
entries.author: Big Beat Studio
entries.what: Two drum machines, sampled classics, a synthesised 808 and Dillo acid bass—our armadillo with the low end. Capture what just happened, recall song FX, edit live and send the mix over USB.

entries.name: Beiwagen
entries.author: Kabelmaier
entries.what: A USB sidecar for the OP-1 Field: the OP-1 streams its four tape tracks to the FM-1, the FM-1 sends a chosen track back as the OP-1's USB input to record, and its keys play the OP-1 over USB-MIDI.
entries.photoAlt: Beiwagen on the FM-1

entries.name: Big Beat Studio BB-BOB
entries.author: Big Beat Studio
entries.what: A Western swing bandstand in your FM1. Call one of 50 classics or hit New Tune and see what the band comes up with, give Leon the steel break, throw in a fill, and bring them back to the theme. Turn Then/Now and the rhythm section picks up acid bass and electronic drums. BB-BOB is standalone FM1 firmware. The product page has the current install instructions.
entries.photoAlt: BB-BOB's launch poster: a cowboy in a yellow suit on a gold disc above the words Big Beat, with the line Bob Wills in your pocket

entries.name: Big Beat Studio BB1
entries.author: TexasRADIO
entries.what: Big Beat Studio BB1 2.0, built on Felucca: two independent drum layers and Dillo acid bass, sharing tape echo and spring reverb. A synthesised 808 and seven sampled machines, 539 rhythm sections including 138 Roland rhythms, and 205 acid bass phrases. Version 2.0 adds a song arranger, ratchets, reversible Evolve, swung recording, a kit builder and 31 additional drum kits. Use its own installer for the application and matched sound library. Release notes document the known audio timing limitation.

entries.name: CHAOS MACHINE
entries.author: DJ Redacted
entries.what: Four generators, circuit, machine, organism, and radio, each with 30 synthesised sounds, that play by themselves and can be played from the keys. It installs from the same browser page as REDACTED, which says it still needs testing on an FM1.

entries.name: ChoralRoot J-6
entries.author: eremansim
entries.what: A fork of Quixotic7's ChoralRoot FM-1 that adds 100 chord sets in the style of the Roland AIRA J-6, with a ready-made chord for each of the twelve notes. It installs from its own browser page or its release package. Its README says it was written entirely by an AI and has not been run on a real FM1, only in tests and an emulator.

entries.name: CHRISTMAS MACHINE
entries.author: DJ Redacted
entries.what: Plays 36 traditional carols in full instrumental arrangements, about an hour of them, with five melody voices to choose from and an organ to play along on the keys. It installs from the same browser page as REDACTED, which says it still needs testing on an FM1.

entries.name: Clavioline
entries.author: MammothCheese
entries.what: Turns the FM-1 into the 1947 Clavioline, an early electronic analog synthesizer. Faithfully rebuilt from the original circuit diagrams with distinctive tone-shaping stops, vibrato, knee-lever expression and vintage electronic sounds.
entries.photoAlt: The FM-1 screen: the tablet rail, the preset, the note, the coupler and the knee lever

entries.name: Compás
entries.author: Big Beat Studio
entries.what: A rhythm section for cumbia, salsa, merengue and bolero: cue the next section and the band lands on it together. Version 1.1 adds a fifth page, KUMBIA, with sounds and patterns from the Hanan Cumbia drum machine, to the 29 groove studies of 1.0, 28 arrangements of written songs, a TR-727 percussion mode, and screens in English or Spanish, which its installer lets you choose. The browser player needs nothing.
entries.photoAlt: Compás on the FM1's screen: a cumbia arrangement at 100 BPM, its band, bass, and percussion levels, and six song parts

entries.name: CONCRÈTE
entries.author: DJ Redacted
entries.what: Four found-sound processes that move across the stereo field, with a dark drone on the keys, a shimmer reverb, and a filtered static wind. It installs from the same browser page as REDACTED, which keeps its earlier versions for going back.

entries.name: Coqui
entries.author: saulofilho
entries.what: A Latin and Caribbean groovebox: congas, bongos, timbales, güiro, clave and cowbell synthesised on the FM1, played by hand or by the sequencer, with a HUMAN knob that loosens the hand. Its README says 1.0 was tested on a real FM1, installed from the official V15 and from another firmware. It installs from its release package and has a browser emulator.

entries.name: COWBELL
entries.author: C0DED00D
entries.what: A cowbell machine after Bad Gear's Volca Cowbell joke, built on M-VAVE's open SDK: a giant MORE knob for ratchets, FEVER for pitch, and PRESCRIPTION choosing one of 13 cowbells sampled from a TR-8S and a DM-10. It installs from its release package with a command-line installer, and a browser page sends the full-quality samples.

entries.name: CRT-4
entries.author: devrvega
entries.what: A four-track groovebox that plays the sound chips of nine game consoles and home computers, with drums on the first track and sixteen sounds per console on the others. The screen is themed to the chosen console. It installs from its own browser page, and a browser emulator lets you try it without an FM1.

entries.name: Dark Funk Durcal Synt
entries.author: Polaris Sound Lab
entries.what: A dark, easy groovebox for acid lines, chopped breaks and warped funk. RITUAL turns two of 15 styles into a full 4-track song with one button, always in key. LIVE adds mutes, stutter, build and drop; NEXT suggests three continuations of your phrase. Tape echo and an eye that feels the music.
entries.photoAlt: Dark Funk Durcal Synt

entries.name: DEEP FIELD
entries.author: Kyle McCann
entries.what: A drone synth with velocity-sensitive keys. Press a key and a voice plays until you stop it: eight voices, thirteen sounds. Motion modes move them in your scale: single notes, chords, chord progressions, arpeggios. Chorus, delay and reverb with freeze. A mixer for drone, lead and effects.

entries.name: DUODRONE
entries.author: pjac1810
entries.what: A two-stylus drone synth after the Dubreq Stylophone CPM DS-2, by SPELLBOX's maker, on foma. All its sounds are synthesised. It installs from its own browser page, which also offers a USB rescue and the way back to M-VAVE's firmware.

entries.name: ECO-1
entries.author: RedtailWorks
entries.what: A plant plays it. Three leaves fire notes as light and water charge them, a stem drones beneath, and rain, wind, gusts and a day and night play the plant. Eight plants, each in its own place.
entries.photoAlt: the FM-1 running ECO-1: a fern on a forest floor, the keys glowing green

entries.name: ENJAMBRE
entries.author: capitanplaneta80-create
entries.what: Felucca with a new engine, ENJAMB, in which insects move as agents through an orbital, quantum or atomic field, so that playing a note collapses or excites the swarm. Its pages are in Spanish. It installs from its own browser page, which also plays it in a browser, and has a web editor.

entries.name: Fernbedienung
entries.author: Kabelmaier
entries.what: Turns the FM-1 into a controller and USB audio interface for the iOS app Steckfeld SF1 on iPad and iPhone: the keys play Steckfeld, the knobs and buttons edit it, and the screen shows the selected module.
entries.photoAlt: Fernbedienung: the FM-1's screens for Steckfeld SF1

entries.name: Finton
entries.author: justynroberts
entries.what: A six-track trance machine after Rollwerk: kick, 909 kit, bass, roller, lead, and pad play over a library of 66 chord progressions, with parameter locks and one knob, LIFT, that runs the build and the drop. It installs from its own browser flasher.

entries.name: FM-1 Neverhood
entries.author: snpwball
entries.what: 22 presets, a four-track sequencer, and a battery indicator, built on fm1-base around The Neverhood: its build takes the game's sprites and sounds from the demo ScummVM offers and samples from Terry Scott Taylor's recordings. Its page plays it in a browser emulator and installs it.

entries.name: FM-KICK
entries.author: David Amo
entries.what: A kick drum synthesizer with a sequencer of up to 32 steps: seven kinds of kick and 48 parameters, p-locks of any parameter on any step, step conditions and chance, nine generators, four LFOs, live and final effects with a hall reverb, three pattern banks, four projects and six themes.
entries.photoAlt: The kick page

entries.name: FM1 Cofrade
entries.author: cotrino
entries.what: A Holy Week firmware built on M-VAVE's FM1 Open V14 SDK, which replaces the sixteen factory projects with original marches for cornets, trumpets, and drums in the style of Semana Santa bands. Its README, in Spanish, says it has been installed and checked on an FM1, though its sounds have not yet been listened to there. Its page plays it in a simulator and installs it over M-VAVE's V15 or Official Open.

entries.name: FM1 Tonic
entries.author: luigirossi-music
entries.what: A drum machine inspired by Sonic Charge’s Microtonic, with an engine of its own and no connection with Sonic Charge: eight synthesised drum voices, a sequencer with accents, fills, and up to 64 steps, 16 patterns a preset chained into songs, an eight-track mixer, reverb, delay, and a master compressor. It has no GitHub release yet. It installs from its own browser page, which can also put M-VAVE’s firmware back, and plays in a browser first.

entries.name: FM1 YOGA
entries.author: Michael Milz
entries.what: A sound companion for Shavasana and meditation. Guided programs on 174, 396, 432 and 528 Hz drift from theta to delta, isochronic for speakers or binaural for headphones, with breath, singing bowls and an ambient garden, then wake you gently. Play handpan, kalimba or chimes on the keys.
entries.photoAlt: The FM-1 with FM1 YOGA: every key and knob labelled

entries.name: GL!TCH
entries.author: saulofilho
entries.what: A neon-noir groovebox built on GR!MM, by Coqui’s maker: four tracks, seven sources, tape and megacity space effects, scales including Insen, Hirajoshi, and Iwato, and 44 factory sounds after Blade Runner, on a glitched landscape that tears with the sound. Its README says 2.0 was tested on a real FM1, and 2.0.2 not yet. It installs from its release package or the FM-1 Firmware Hub, and plays in a browser emulator.

entries.name: GLIDER
entries.author: ttreu
entries.what: A drone synthesiser built on M-VAVE's FM1 Open: white keys latch scale tones, black keys glide them, with a tape echo, ladder filter, shimmer reverb and a quiet microsound drum track. It installs from its own browser page, and a browser simulator is available. The README says it has run on one FM1 and no licence is stated on GitHub.

entries.name: GRAV-1
entries.author: RedtailWorks
entries.what: A star and its planets. Slow, dark, spacey ambient: a star of coloured noise and up to six planets, each a voice playing round its orbit. Bigger planets swell smaller ones; dust, asteroids and comets drift through.
entries.photoAlt: the FM-1 running GRAV-1: a gold star and its planets on their orbits, the keys glowing gold

entries.name: GRIDLIGHT
entries.author: pjac1810
entries.what: A 16 × 16 light-grid sequencer instrument after Yamaha's Tenori-On, by SPELLBOX's maker, on foma, with a song of 16 blocks saved to flash. All its sounds are synthesised. It installs from its own browser page.

entries.name: Groove OS
entries.author: Peter Gombos
entries.what: An eight-track groovebox that keeps an FM synth and adds a virtual analogue synth and drum kits, with a 64-step sequencer with parameter locks, a six-effect mixer, and a performance mode with scenes. Version 2.0 adds a sampler that records from a phone over Bluetooth or USB, or from the FM1 itself, Bluetooth audio, and a wider stereo mix; 1.4 owners update to it free. It installs from its own browser page, which can also put M-VAVE's V15 back, and has a browser emulator to try first.
entries.photoAlt: Groove OS's tracks screen, with drum, acid, and FM tracks

entries.name: Hookology
entries.author: bendawsonjr
entries.what: A Melodee 1.6.1 fork for catching an idea fast, as a chord, a strum, a loop, or a hook, with HERA’s chord sets and features after SLOOP. It installs from its own browser page, which backs the FM1 up first and can put M-VAVE’s V15 back.

entries.name: Impressionism
entries.author: darrenjaworski
entries.what: A generative ambient firmware in which voices drift on their own slow timers inside Impressionist harmony: whole-tone and pentatonic scales, extended and quartal chords, and planing over a pedal tone. It is built to drift rather than be played. It installs from its release package, and can be tried in a browser emulator first. Its README does not say whether it has been tried on an FM1.

entries.name: Kurzhaar
entries.author: kurzhaar168
entries.what: A monophonic bass synth and step sequencer on Dinghy, named for a German Shorthaired Pointer: two oscillators and a sub into a resonant ladder filter, two LFOs, drive and reverb, 16 presets, and 16 patterns in your key and scale, with MIDI clock sync and recording over USB audio. It installs from its release package with a command-line installer.

entries.name: LATIN ORGAN
entries.author: DJ Redacted
entries.what: A two-bar Latin-rock percussion loop with a cabasa, and an eight-voice tonewheel-style organ played on the keys, with drive, a rotary effect, and reverb. It installs from the same browser page as REDACTED, which says it still needs testing on an FM1.

entries.name: LAUNCHPARTY
entries.author: megagott
entries.what: MYCELIUM's sibling: playable synth sounds with lightshows on a Novation Launchpad Pro MK3, triggered from the FM1's keys. A browser companion previews shows and updates the firmware, which installs from its release package.

entries.name: LOF-1
entries.author: RedtailWorks
entries.what: A lofi groovebox. You play the lead and a tired jazz band follows: comp, bass and drums move with your chords, an Answer voice replies, and a record, cassette, reel or radio sits under it all.
entries.photoAlt: the FM-1 running LOF-1: a record turning, a Cmaj7 chord, the keys glowing peach

entries.name: Maestro
entries.author: node56
entries.what: Music lessons on the FM1’s screen, with note-reading, rhythm, and sight-reading drills graded on pitch and timing; its later builds add FM piano sounds and a sheet-music recorder. Built on Dinghy over Felucca, it installs from its own browser page as a test build, while its README still calls the on-device side a scaffold.

entries.name: Mario Texture's GRANA
entries.author: mongio
entries.what: A granular sample player in the spirit of the MicroGranny 2, with four sample layers, lo-fi effects, an arpeggiator, a sequencer and 64 named presets. It installs through an editor page in its release, which also loads your own samples, or from the release packages. The README says it was tested on a real FM1, and its interface is in Italian.

entries.name: MASIF
entries.author: thecemeterygates
entries.what: A four-track sample tracker and rack sampler built on zp12, SLOOP, Felucca, and Ketch: 128 instruments with tables, grooves, and modulation, 24 samples in about 730 KB, and a sampler page on the FM1 that records the computer's sound over USB. Its web page prepares samples, syncs them to the FM1, and backs it up. It installs from its release package.

entries.name: MORSE
entries.author: Da-Wei Lee
entries.what: Learn and use Morse code. Key on the piano keys (straight key or iambic paddles) and see what you sent, drill short and long presses, learn by sound with flash cards, listen to endless practice, type letters and CW phrases on the keys. Keying goes out over USB-MIDI in the Vail format.
entries.photoAlt: MORSE on the FM-1

entries.name: MOSS-1
entries.author: Theo Wecker
entries.what: Ambient firmware: lofi chords, nature scenes and generative pads and bells, each with its own pixel picture. Play and the music follows: notes loop in an eight layer looper, each layer in its own voice. Build any chord progression or play whole chords live, program your own drums and a bass line…

entries.name: MT-40X
entries.author: altessproduction
entries.what: A Casio MT-40 clone on Felucca, with its notes in French: the six 1981 accompaniment rhythms, among them ROCK, the pattern behind the Sleng Teng riddim, with four drum lanes, a bass that follows a one-key chord, FILL, A/B variation, and swing, while Felucca's engines stay playable on the keys. Its alpha release carries a package for Felucca's web installer, and it plays in a browser emulator.

entries.name: NJA TACK
entries.author: NjamesZ
entries.what: A Felucca-derived firmware of moving harmony and played MIDI. Its README calls 6.28-rc5 an experimental review candidate, installed once on an FM1 on 10 Nov, with its listening, timing, and recovery tests still open. It installs from its release package.

entries.name: ObsSynth
entries.author: orianbsilva
entries.what: A four-voice synth built on Hortator, after the ObsSynth desktop instruments: two oscillators with standard, supersaw, wavetable, and granular engines, a sub, noise, sync and ring modulation, a multimode filter, two envelopes, two LFOs, and poly, mono, legato, and unison modes. Its README says 0.1.0 was tested on an FM1. It installs from its release package, and plays in a browser first.

entries.name: ObsSynth FM-1
entries.author: Orian Beltrame
entries.what: A four-voice synthesizer: two oscillators per voice, each STD (8 waves), SUPER (7 detuned saws, squares, triangles or sines), WT or GRAIN; a 12/24 dB multimode filter, two ADSRs, two LFOs, unison, delay, reverb and chorus. 16 factory presets, 16 of yours. Play it in the browser first.
entries.photoAlt: The FM-1 screen on the WAVES preset

entries.name: OCTODRONE
entries.author: pjac1810
entries.what: An eight-voice drone synth after the SOMA Laboratory Lyra-8, by SPELLBOX's maker, on foma, with eight panels saved to flash. All its sounds are synthesised. It installs from its own browser page.

entries.name: OpenIFW
entries.author: rcell233
entries.what: A port of OpenIFW’s monophonic synthesiser, with four oscillators, two main filters, two LFOs, and a full effects chain. It installs from its own browser page, which also plays it in a demo, and its notes are in Chinese.

entries.name: OrGigs
entries.author: Bobo
entries.what: It's an organ. Three manuals with 84 free-running tone generators and no voice stealing, eight models from tonewheel and combo organs to pipe organs and free reeds, drawbars, percussion, rotary, drive, delay and reverb, 16 performance setups, three MIDI zones and Yamaha SEQTRAK control.

entries.name: PaperLagoon
entries.author: hacha
entries.what: A generative ambient firmware. FM voices through a tape echo and a plate play by themselves in seven worlds that exist nowhere. You steer from outside: a key offers something to a hidden state, the knobs change the weather, and the music answers slowly.
entries.photoAlt: PaperLagoon

entries.name: PHREAK
entries.author: dagnazty
entries.what: A six-track groovebox on SLOOP, with three synth tracks and three drum tracks whose kits come from a USB stick. Its release carries a firmware package, installed from a computer over USB, and a web installer. Its README calls it a personal fork tested on one FM1, and says it keeps your projects, presets, samples and settings and can go back to SLOOP or the official firmware.

entries.name: Plissken
entries.author: dustekin
entries.what: A John Carpenter-inspired soundtrack sketch: the keyboard plays Juno, piano, Pro-1, guitar, bass, CS-50 and CS-80-style sounds, chords, and Linn LM-1 drum samples, with an arpeggiator, a phrase recorder, and a five-track visual sequencer that saves up to 16 songs. Its maker calls it a prototype and says it has been played on an FM1. It installs from the.fwsc package on its release page, following the Firmware Hub's install steps with a bootloader.

entries.name: Prysm
entries.author: NicholasPratt
entries.what: A four-voice wavetable FM synthesizer built on Dinghy and Felucca: two oscillators a voice, each a chain of three wavetable operators that modulate by FM, ring, or mix, with a resonant filter, an LFO, a looping modulation envelope, chorus, delay, plate reverb, and eight patch slots. It installs from its own browser page, which since 0.8 also has an editor that plays Prysm in the page and stays in step with a connected FM1. Version 0.9 added a polyphonic sequencer that records live, and 1.0 VCA OPEN, which holds the amp open for a drone.

entries.name: QUADRO
entries.author: matttallison
entries.what: A four-section performance synthesiser after the ARP Quadra: a bass, a string ensemble, a polyphonic synth and a two-voice lead play at once across a split keyboard, through a 14-stage phase shifter, reverb and delay. It has one-finger chords with a bass root, and a sequencer over the keys you hold that syncs to MIDI clock. It installs from its release package.

entries.name: Quod
entries.author: tulpasoftworks
entries.what: A drone instrument of thirteen sine voices that flow towards the note you play, an angel cluster above the root and a demon cluster below it, with a Heaven / Hell knob. It also runs on a Mac as an Audio Unit instrument, and its FM1 firmware is in its release package.

entries.name: REDACTED
entries.author: DJ Redacted
entries.what: An experimental four-track lo-fi groovebox built on Felucca: ALGORITHM picks the track, and four knobs set its fracture, static, chance, and mutate. It installs from its own browser page, which offers 0.1 as a known-working rollback because hardware testing of 0.2 is still pending.

entries.name: RIDDIM ROOTS
entries.author: tskorbenko
entries.what: A generative reggae and dub band: six players (drums and percussion, bass, skank, organ, horns and lead, and piano) across 11 styles from ska to dub techno, with an Evolve control and transitions that do not stop the music. Its README, in Ukrainian, says it is built on M-VAVE’s FM1 Open SDK. It has no release; its.fwsc package is in the repository.

entries.name: ROM-1
entries.author: devrvega
entries.what: A sixteen-part sound module, as the rack modules of the nineties were: a part for each MIDI channel, each playing a preset of sounds you choose, with a filter, envelopes, reverb, and chorus. It plays.sf2 files. It installs from its own browser page and can be tried in a browser first.

entries.name: Ruido
entries.author: Miguel Hernández Domenech
entries.what: 4-oscillator drone synthesizer with coupled Schmitt-trigger oscillators, per-voice dual Sallen-Key resonant HPF-to-LPF filters, 8 audio-rate LFOs, circular scene morphing, and 3 pressure-sensitive keyboards (Live Mixer, Circuit Lab, Rhythm Lab) with a live CRT oscilloscope.

entries.name: SAMSARA
entries.author: Tomorrow's Man
entries.what: A slow generative ambient piece that plays itself for hours and never repeats: a choir pad, soft bells, a gliding bass and a rare low ground drift through harmonies and colours like weather. Four pieces, four knobs to tend it (Mood, Density, Drift, Space). A fork of AMB-1.
entries.photoAlt: SAMSARA's screen: the Tide page

entries.name: Selva1
entries.author: deabrewcontato-code
entries.what: A synth inspired by São Paulo, with three wavetable, analog, FM, or noise oscillators, a ladder filter, a modulation matrix, and a 303-style sequencer. The same engine runs in a browser and as a plugin; the FM1 version is built on SLOOP and installs from its own page. Its notes are in Portuguese.

entries.name: SQRL-1
entries.author: hed0rah
entries.what: A fork of Felucca with a shell of its own, built around pairs: a SOUND that makes the tone (FM6, LIZARD, SHOCK, DRUMS, MOUTH, ANALOG, PHASE, or PHYS) and a NOTE engine that chooses the notes (KEYS, CHORD, RUDIMENT, LINES, ALIVE, and more). Hold HOME and the octave becomes a wheel for picking the pair. It installs from its release package.

entries.name: Stamp Composer
entries.author: MichaelAPerry
entries.what: A Mario Paint-style music composer: stamp characters on a staff to write songs with 31 Mario Paint sounds, eight layers, flats and triplets, swing, and bar editing. It has per-sound MIDI out, clock sync, eight song slots with autosave, and a Twinkle Twinkle demo song, and installs from its own page. The sounds and sprites come from Super Mario Paint, a separate asset pack with its own notice.

entries.name: SynthMaven
entries.author: KingXeryus
entries.what: A Melodee-based groovebox for oriental live music, with a song arranger of up to 16 sections and engines such as DX7, Juno, and acid beside Melodee's own. It installs from its own browser page and has a web editor and an illustrated guide.

entries.name: VNL-1
entries.author: pianomansam
entries.what: A generative lo-fi DJ groovebox: endless, complete songs built with music theory, each with its own key, chords, layout and six-part band (drums, bass, accompaniment, lead, pad, texture). Let it play, or shape the songs live.
entries.photoAlt: The simple home screen: a spinning record beside the song, its key, chord, section and tempo

entries.name: Yanfei
entries.author: izumoe
entries.what: A fork of Felucca with twelve engines, 96 factory presets and a four-track tracker. It installs from the browser installer on its own website, which also has an editor and an emulator. It has no GitHub releases, and its README does not say whether it has been tried on an FM1.
